definition_zh: 货币的；金融的；（政策上）与货币供给和利率有关的；以货币计值的
definition_en: relating to money, to the supply of money in an economy, or to values expressed in money
core_image: 一间造币厂的车间，成排的圆片在传送带上被压成一样的重量与成色
scene: 央行会议室里，几位官员盯着利率曲线，讨论是否收紧银根。Monetary policy tightened before the currency lost half its value.
sceneCN: 这里 monetary 指「与货币供给和利率相关的政策层面」（第 2 个义项：作为政策领域）；句意为在货币贬值一半之前，货币政策先收紧了。

pos.zh: 货币的；金融的；以货币计值的

derivatives.zh: 拉丁 moneta（造币厂）经古法语 moneie → 钱；货币
monetary + -ism（主义）→ 货币主义（语义偏移：从属性转到学派）
monetarism + -ist（信奉者）→ 货币主义者
moneta + -ize → 货币化；铸成货币（语义偏移：从造币转到变现）
古英语 mynet（硬币）→ 造币厂；铸造（同族不同线）

senses.title: Relating to money as a medium
senses.titleCN: 与作为交换媒介的货币有关
senses.definition: concerned with money as the medium of exchange, including units, coins and notes
senses.definitionCN: 涉及作为交换媒介的货币，含单位、硬币与纸币
senses.example: The two states agreed to use a common monetary unit.
senses.exampleCN: 两国同意使用共同的货币单位。
senses.why: Moneta was the mint, so the adjective first describes anything belonging to coin and currency.
senses.whyCN: Moneta 是造币厂，因此这个形容词最初描述一切属于硬币与通货之物。

senses.title: Relating to the money supply as policy
senses.titleCN: 与货币供给的政策层面有关
senses.definition: concerned with the quantity of money, interest rates and central-bank action
senses.definitionCN: 涉及货币数量、利率与中央银行行动
senses.example: Monetary policy tightened before the currency lost half its value.
senses.exampleCN: 在货币贬值一半之前，货币政策先收紧了。
senses.why: Once the state manages the mint, the adjective attaches to the decisions made there.
senses.whyCN: 一旦国家管理造币厂，这个形容词就附到在那里做出的决策上。

senses.title: Expressed or valued in money
senses.definition: measured, stated or compared in money terms rather than in kind
senses.definitionCN: 以货币而非实物来衡量、表述或比较
senses.example: The loss was small in monetary terms and large in reputation.
senses.exampleCN: 以货币计算损失不大，以声誉计算损失很大。
senses.why: Anything the mint measures can be described as measured by the mint's unit.
senses.whyCN: 凡是造币厂所计量的，都可用造币厂的单位来描述。

senses.title: Of a mint, in historical use
senses.titleCN: 与造币厂有关的（历史用法）
senses.definition: historical: belonging to a mint, its officers or its operations
senses.definitionCN: 历史用法：属于造币厂、其官员或其作业的
senses.example: The monetary records of the abbey list every die and every officer.
senses.exampleCN: 修道院的铸币记录列出了每一副模具与每一名官员。
senses.why: The oldest sense is literally 'of the mint', before the word widened to money in general.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项字面上就是「造币厂的」，之后才扩展到泛指货币。

senses.title: Paid in money rather than in kind
senses.definition: consisting of money, as a payment, prize or compensation
senses.definitionCN: 由钱构成的，如付款、奖金或赔偿
senses.example: The settlement included a monetary award and an apology.
senses.exampleCN: 和解方案包括一笔金钱赔偿与一份道歉。
senses.why: A payment is a use of the mint's product, so any cash component can carry the label.
senses.whyCN: 付款是造币厂产物的使用，因此任何现金部分都可带上这个标签。

senses.title: Of a shared currency area
senses.definition: describing a group of states that share one currency and one rate-setting authority
senses.definitionCN: 描述共用一种货币与一个定息当局的一组国家
senses.example: A monetary union without a common budget is fragile.
senses.exampleCN: 没有共同预算的货币联盟是脆弱的。
senses.why: If a unit can be shared, the adjective can name the arrangement that shares it.
senses.whyCN: 若一种单位可被共用，这个形容词就能指共用它的那种安排。

senses.title: Moved by money as a motive
senses.definition: concerned with money as a reason for action rather than as a measure
senses.definitionCN: 把金钱当作行动理由，而非计量尺度
senses.example: Their objections were monetary, not scientific.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的反对出于钱，而非出于科学。
senses.why: The adjective shifts from the instrument to the motive behind using it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从工具转到使用工具背后的动机。

senses.title: Contrasted with fiscal in economics
senses.definition: in economics, marking the central-bank side of policy as distinct from taxation and spending
senses.definitionCN: 在经济学中，标出政策中的央行一侧，与税收和支出相对
senses.example: The textbook separates monetary from fiscal tools in one chapter.
senses.exampleCN: 这本教科书用一章把货币工具与财政工具分开。
senses.why: Two arms of policy need two labels, and the mint supplies the name for one of them.
senses.whyCN: 政策的两只手臂需要两个标签，造币厂为其中一只提供了名称。

intro.en: Monetary goes back to the title of a Roman goddess whose temple held the mint, and the word for a place became the word for money itself.
intro.cn: monetary 回到一位罗马女神的称号，她的神庙设有造币厂；一个指场所的词就此成了指货币的词。

items.en: Moneta was an epithet of Juno, in whose temple on the Capitoline Hill the Roman mint stood; moneta came to mean both the mint and the money made there.
items.cn: Moneta 是朱诺的称号，罗马造币厂就设在卡比托利欧山上的她的神庙中；moneta 由此兼指造币厂与在那里造出的钱。

items.en: Why Juno carried the name Moneta is uncertain; the common link to monere 'to warn' is a hypothesis based on the goddess's advisory role, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: 朱诺为何带有 Moneta 之名，来源不确定；把它与 monere「警告」相联系的通行说法，是基于这位女神的告诫职能提出的假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Monetarius meant 'of the mint' and also 'a moneyer', the official who struck coin; the adjective in English descends from this form.
items.cn: monetarius 意为「造币厂的」，也指「铸币官」，即冲压硬币的官员；英语中的形容词由这一形式而来。

items.en: Old French moneie and Middle English money carry the substance sense, while the adjective follows the learned Latin line and keeps the -ary ending.
items.cn: 古法语 moneie 与中古英语 money 承载「钱财」这一实体义，而形容词走学术拉丁那条线，保留了 -ary 词尾。

items.en: Late and medieval Latin use monetarius for anything concerning coinage, including taxes paid in coin, which is how the adjective widens beyond the building.
items.cn: 晚期与中世纪拉丁用 monetarius 指一切与铸币有关之物，包括以硬币缴纳的税，这个形容词由此越出建筑之外。

items.en: In the twentieth century monetary becomes a technical term opposed to fiscal, naming the central bank's tools rather than the treasury's.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，monetary 成为与 fiscal 相对的技术术语，指央行的工具而非财政部的工具。

note.en: The first group shares the money root or a similar shape; the second holds adjectives from neighbouring economic domains.
note.cn: 第一组共享货币词根或外形相近；第二组是邻近经济领域的形容词。

entries.definition: The thing itself, from the same mint word by the French route; monetary is the adjective built on the Latin line.
entries.definitionCN: 指钱本身，经法语路径出自同一个造币厂词；monetary 是建于拉丁那条线的形容词。

entries.definition: A person who holds a theory about the money supply; the adjective describes the domain, the noun describes a school.
entries.definitionCN: 持某种货币供给理论的人；形容词描述领域，名词描述学派。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to convert into currency or to earn revenue from something; not merely 'to be about money'.
entries.definitionCN: 意为转为货币或从某物取得收入，并非仅仅是「与钱有关」。

entries.definition: Meaning warning or admonitory, from monere 'to warn'; it looks like monetary but shares no money sense.
entries.definitionCN: 意为告诫的，来自 monere「警告」；外形像 monetary，但完全不含货币义。

entries.definition: Relating to finance, including banks, markets and corporate accounts; monetary is narrower and centres on currency and the central bank.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及金融，含银行、市场与企业账目；monetary 更窄，以货币与央行为中心。

entries.definition: Relating to government revenue and spending; economics pairs it with monetary as the two levers of policy.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及政府收入与支出；经济学把它与 monetary 并列为政策的两根杠杆。

entries.definition: A formal word for 'relating to money', chiefly in legal writing about pecuniary loss or advantage.
entries.definitionCN: 指「与钱有关的」的正式用词，主要见于法律写作中的金钱损失或利益。

entries.definition: Relating to the economy as a whole, including production and employment; monetary covers only the currency side.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及整体经济，含生产与就业；monetary 仅涵盖货币那一面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Moneta was the mint in Juno's temple: monetary means of the mint, then of money.
normal.cn: Moneta 是朱诺神庙里的造币厂：monetary 先是「造币厂的」，再是「货币的」。

normal.en: The family runs money, monetary, monetarism, monetarist, monetize, monetization, mint.
normal.cn: 同族词有 money、monetary、monetarism、monetarist、monetize、monetization、mint。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the fields: monetary policy, monetary union, monetary value, monetary compensation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分领域：货币政策、货币联盟、货币价值、金钱赔偿。

normal.en: In economics the pair is monetary and fiscal: the central bank against the treasury.
normal.cn: 经济学中的成对术语是 monetary 与 fiscal：央行对财政部。

normal.en: The false friend monitory warns, and it comes from the verb to warn, not from the mint.
normal.cn: 假朋友 monitory 意为告诫，来自「警告」那个动词，与造币厂无关。

abstract.en: Picture rows of identical discs weighed on one scale, all judged by the same number.
abstract.cn: 想象成排同样的圆片放在一杆秤上，全由同一个数字来评判。

abstract.en: Picture a committee raising a rate and watching prices fall a month later.
abstract.cn: 想象一个委员会抬高利率，一个月后看着物价下跌。

abstract.en: Picture a settlement paid in notes, with an apology added because the notes were not enough.
abstract.cn: 想象一笔以纸币支付的和解，因为纸币不够，又添上一份道歉。

examples.en: The country entered a monetary union and lost the right to set its own rate.
examples.cn: 这个国家加入货币联盟，失去了自行定息的权利。

examples.en: In monetary terms the rescue was cheap; in human terms it was not.
examples.cn: 以金钱计算，这次救援很便宜；以人的代价计算，并不便宜。

examples.en: Monetary and fiscal policy pulled in opposite directions all year.
examples.cn: 货币政策与财政政策整年都在往相反方向拉。

dict_mnemonic.text: moneta（造币厂）+ ary（…的）＝ 造币厂那一套的；先记「一间厂」，再记「一套政策」。

root: 拉丁 moneta（朱诺称号，其神庙设造币厂，由此兼指造币厂与钱币）+ -arius（属于…的）→ 晚期拉丁 monetarius → 英语 monetary；Moneta 与 monere「警告」的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start at a mint building and end at a policy label: money as medium, the money supply, value in money, the historical mint, payment in cash, a currency area, money as motive, and the economics pairing with fiscal.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一间造币厂开始，落到一个政策标签：作为媒介的货币、货币供给、以钱计值、历史上的造币厂、现金支付、货币区、金钱动机，以及经济学中与财政并列的一侧。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mint where every disc is weighed to the same standard, and that single number then judges everything else.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间造币厂把每枚圆片都称到同一标准，而那一个数字随后评判其余一切。

branches.en: PLACE AND MEDIUM: the building and its officers first, then the money they make as a medium of exchange.
branches.cn: 场所与媒介：先是建筑与官员，再是他们造出的作为交换媒介的钱。

branches.en: MANAGED SUPPLY: a state that runs the mint also sets the rate, and states that share a rate form a union.
branches.cn: 被管理的供给：经营造币厂的国家也定利率，共用利率的国家则组成联盟。

branches.en: MEASURE AND PAYMENT: anything can be priced in the unit, and anything can be paid in it.
branches.cn: 计量与支付：任何东西都可用这个单位标价，也都可用它支付。

branches.en: MONEY AS REASON: the instrument becomes a motive when people object on monetary grounds.
branches.cn: 钱作为理由：当人们以钱为由反对时，工具就成了动机。

branches.en: ONE OF TWO LEVERS: economics needs a name for the central-bank arm as against the treasury.
branches.cn: 两根杠杆之一：经济学需要给央行这只手臂一个与财政部相对的名称。

intro.en: Monetary is a Latin adjective of the mint, and the root behind it also gives the plain English noun for money and the vocabulary of monetary theory.
intro.cn: monetary 是一个指造币厂的拉丁形容词，其词根还给出英语中指钱的普通名词与货币理论的整套词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin moneta 'mint, money' gives money through French and monetary, monetize and monetarism through the learned line. The related verb monere 'to warn' gives monitory, which is a different word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 moneta「造币厂、钱」经法语给出 money，经学术线给出 monetary、monetize 与 monetarism。相关动词 monere「警告」给出 monitory，那是另一个词。

items.example: The root names the place before it names the money.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根先指场所，再指钱。

items.structure: monetarius (Latin adjective and noun, 'of the mint; moneyer')
items.example: The Latin adjective supplies the English form.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁形容词提供英语形式。

items.example: The suffix marks relation rather than substance.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标出关系，而非实体。

items.example: The adjective is the learned member of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是家族中的学术成员。

items.example: The plain noun came by the French route.
items.exampleCN: 这个普通名词是经法语路径来的。

items.example: The verb extends the mint to any source of revenue.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把造币厂扩展到任何收入来源。

items.meaning: a theory of the money supply
items.example: The suffix turns an adjective into a school.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成学派。

items.example: The person form follows the doctrine form.
items.exampleCN: 人称形式跟在学说形式之后。

items.example: The look-alike comes from the verb to warn, not from the mint.
items.exampleCN: 这个形近词来自「警告」那个动词，与造币厂无关。

definition_zh: 显示器；监测仪；班长；监督者；监测；监控；监听
definition_en: a device that displays or records information, a person who warns or keeps order, or to watch and check something continuously over time
core_image: 一个站在旁边不断提醒“注意”的人，眼睛一直盯着同一处
scene: 控制室里，工程师盯着显示管道压力的监视器。From the control room the engineer watched the monitor that showed the pressure inside the pipeline.
sceneCN: 这里 monitor 是「显示器」（第 1 个义项：显示画面或数据的屏幕）；句意：工程师在控制室里盯着显示管道内压力的显示器。场景要点：昏暗的控制室、一排亮着的屏幕、屏幕上跳动的压力曲线、管道剖面图；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 显示器；监测仪；班长；监督者；告诫者
监测；监控；监听；跟踪观察

senses.title: A screen that shows the picture
senses.definition: a screen, especially a computer or television display, that shows information or a picture
senses.definitionCN: 显示信息或画面的屏幕，尤指电脑或电视显示屏
senses.example: The second monitor shows the camera feed from the front door.
senses.exampleCN: 第二块显示器显示前门的摄像头画面。
senses.why: Broadcasting used a monitor for a device that continuously checked a transmission, and the screen showing that check took the name. A computer display repeats the role: it lets someone keep watch on what the machine is doing.
senses.whyCN: 广播业曾把持续检查传输质量的设备称为 monitor，显示这项检查的屏幕便沿用了这个名字。电脑显示器重复着同一角色：让人持续看清机器在做什么。

senses.title: An instrument that keeps watch
senses.definition: a device that continuously measures and displays a physical condition, such as heart rate or pressure
senses.definitionCN: 持续测量并显示某项身体或物理状况的设备，如心率或压力
senses.example: The heart monitor began to beep faster and faster.
senses.exampleCN: 心脏监测仪开始越响越快地鸣叫。
senses.why: The Latin monitor was a person who warned. An instrument that watches a pulse and sounds an alarm takes over the warning job, so the person's title passes to the machine.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 monitor 是一个发出警告的人。一台盯着脉搏、并发出警报的仪器接过了这份警告的职责，于是人的称呼转移到了机器上。

senses.title: The pupil who keeps order
senses.definition: a senior pupil at a school given the task of keeping order or checking attendance
senses.definitionCN: 学校里被赋予维持秩序或检查出勤任务的高年级学生
senses.example: The hall monitor checked the corridors every hour.
senses.exampleCN: 走廊值日生每小时巡查一次走廊。
senses.why: This is the oldest English sense, from 1540s: a senior pupil 'charged with keeping order'. The student does exactly what the Latin word says — reminds others of the rules and reports breaches.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语里最古老的义项，始于 16 世纪 40 年代：受命维持秩序的高年级学生。这个学生做的正是拉丁词所说的——提醒别人守规矩，并报告违规。

senses.title: An official who warns
senses.definition: a person appointed to observe, advise, and warn, especially in an official or technical role
senses.definitionCN: 受指派观察、建议并提出告诫的人，尤指担任正式或技术职务者
senses.example: A monitor was appointed to warn the committee about conflicts of interest.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会任命了一名监督员，就利益冲突提出告诫。
senses.why: Latin monitor meant 'one who reminds, admonishes, or checks', and also 'an overseer, instructor, guide'. The English noun keeps that advisory, warning figure before it ever names a machine.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 monitor 意为“提醒者、告诫者、检查者”，也指“监督者、指导者、引路人”。英语名词先保留了这个提出建议与警告的人，之后才用它命名机器。

senses.title: Watch the numbers over time
senses.definition: to measure and check a quantity or condition regularly over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间内定期测量并检查某个数量或状况
senses.example: Sensors monitor the temperature of the tank every ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器每十分钟监测一次储罐的温度。
senses.why: The verb appeared in 1924 for checking the quality of radio signals. Its core is repetition: a monitor does not look once but keeps looking, so the verb means sustained checking rather than a single glance.
senses.whyCN: 动词于 1924 年出现，指检查无线电信号的质量。它的核心是重复：monitor 不是看一眼，而是持续地看，所以这个动词表示持续的检查，而不是一瞥。

senses.title: Keep someone under surveillance
senses.definition: to watch a person, group, or activity closely, especially to detect wrongdoing or risk
senses.definitionCN: 密切注视某人、某群体或某项活动，尤为了发现不当行为或风险
senses.example: The company monitors its drivers' speed and braking through an app.
senses.exampleCN: 公司通过一个应用监控司机的车速与刹车情况。
senses.why: When the watching is turned from a gauge to people, the warning role becomes surveillance. The same continuous attention is now aimed at behaviour that may need correcting.
senses.whyCN: 当注视的对象从仪表转向人，提醒的职责就变成了监控。同样的持续关注，现在对准了可能需要纠正的行为。

senses.title: Listen to a channel
senses.definition: to listen to a radio, telephone, or other channel continuously in order to catch particular information
senses.definitionCN: 持续收听无线电、电话或其他频道，以捕捉特定信息
senses.example: They monitored the radio channel all night, waiting for a reply.
senses.exampleCN: 他们整夜监听那个无线电频道，等待回复。
senses.why: The earliest verb sense was exactly this: checking radio signals for quality. Listening to a channel is watching with the ears, and the word's continuity remains.
senses.whyCN: 最早的动词义正是这个：检查无线电信号的质量。用耳朵听一个频道就是“用耳朵看”，而这个词的持续性仍然保留。

senses.title: The lizard that warns
senses.definition: a large lizard of the family Varanidae, called a monitor because of an old story that it warned people of crocodiles
senses.definitionCN: 巨蜥科的大型蜥蜴，因古老传说称它会向人预警鳄鱼而得名
senses.example: A monitor lizard crossed the trail and disappeared into the grass.
senses.exampleCN: 一只巨蜥穿过小径，消失在草丛里。
senses.why: The name was given in 1826 because the lizard was fabled to give warning of Nile crocodiles. It is the same 'warner' sense, applied to an animal rather than a person or device.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字始于 1826 年，因为传说这种蜥蜴会预警尼罗河鳄鱼。它仍是“警告者”这层意思，只是用在了动物身上，而不是人或设备。

senses.title: The ironclad that admonished
senses.definition: the name of the first ironclad warship of that design, built in 1862 and intended as a warning to the Confederacy
senses.definitionCN: 1862 年建造的第一艘该型铁甲舰的名称，意在向南方邦联发出警告
senses.example: The Monitor fought the Merrimack in 1862 and changed naval warfare.
senses.exampleCN: 1862 年，莫尼特号与梅里马克号交战，改变了海战方式。
senses.why: The inventor chose the name because the ship was meant to 'admonish' Confederate leaders. The Latin warner becomes a floating threat, a warning made of iron.
senses.whyCN: 发明者选择这个名字，是因为这艘船意在“告诫”南方邦联的领导人。拉丁语的告诫者变成了浮在水上的威胁，一个用铁铸成的警告。

senses.title: A background watcher in software
senses.titleCN: 软件中的后台监控程序
senses.definition: in computing, a program or process that runs in the background and checks system activity
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机领域，指在后台运行、检查系统活动的程序或进程
senses.example: A background monitor logs every login and flags unusual hours.
senses.exampleCN: 一个后台监控程序记录每次登录，并标记异常时段。
senses.why: Software repeats the human watchman: it runs unnoticed, checks continuously, and reports what looks wrong. The old 'one who warns' is now a loop of code.
senses.whyCN: 软件重复着人类更夫的角色：它不声不响地运行，持续检查，并报告看起来不对的地方。古老的“告诫者”如今成了一段循环的代码。

intro.en: Monitor began as a Latin word for a person who warns, entered English in the sixteenth century as a school officer, and only in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries became a machine, a lizard, a warship, and finally a screen. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: monitor 最初是拉丁语中表示“告诫者”的词，16 世纪作为学校职务进入英语，直到 19 与 20 世纪才变成仪器、蜥蜴、军舰，最后成为屏幕。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'senior pupil at a school charged with keeping order'. It came from Latin monitor.
items.cn: 英语最早记录为“受命维持秩序的学校高年级学生”。它来自拉丁语 monitor。

items.en: Latin monitor meant 'one who reminds, admonishes, or checks', and also 'an overseer, instructor, guide, teacher'. It was an agent noun from monere.
items.cn: 拉丁语 monitor 意为“提醒者、告诫者、检查者”，也指“监督者、指导者、引路人、教师”。它是 monere 的施动名词。

items.en: Monere meant 'to remind, bring to one's recollection, tell of; admonish, advise, warn, instruct, teach'. It goes back to PIE *moneie-, a causative form of *men- 'to think', the root also behind Latin memini 'I remember' and mens 'mind'.
items.cn: monere 意为“提醒、使想起、告知；告诫、建议、警告、指导、教导”。它可追溯到原始印欧语 *moneie-，即 *men-“思考”的使役形式；同一词根也是拉丁语 memini“我记得”与 mens“心智”的来源。

items.en: The monitor lizard was so called because it was fabled to warn people of Nile crocodiles (1826). The ironclad warship Monitor (1862) was named by its inventor because it was meant to 'admonish' Confederate leaders.
items.cn: 巨蜥被称为 monitor，是因为传说它会向人预警尼罗河鳄鱼（1826）。铁甲舰莫尼特号（1862）由发明者命名，因为这艘船意在“告诫”南方邦联的领导人。

items.en: The verb is recorded in 1924 meaning 'to check for quality', originally of radio signals. The general sense 'observe, keep under review' is from 1944. Keats had used it in 1818 to mean 'to guide'.
items.cn: 动词于 1924 年有记录，意为“检查质量”，最初用于无线电信号。泛指“观察、持续审视”的义项始于 1944 年。济慈在 1818 年曾用它表示“引导”。

items.en: A broadcasting sense, 'a device to continuously check on the technical quality of a transmission', is recorded from 1931 and led to the sense 'a TV screen displaying the picture from a particular camera'. The computer display is a later extension of that screen sense.
items.cn: 广播义“持续检查传输技术质量的设备”记录于 1931 年，并由此引出“显示某一摄像机画面的电视屏幕”这一义项。电脑显示器是该屏幕义的后期引申。

note.en: The first group separates the noun and adjective forms built on monitor from two related warning words; the second compares the verbs of watching that learners use interchangeably.
note.cn: 第一组把由 monitor 构成的名词与形容词形式，同两个相关的“警告”词分开；第二组比较学习者常互换使用的几个“看管”动词。

entries.definition: the continuous act of checking or watching something. It is the process, while monitor is the device or the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 持续检查或观察的行为。它是过程，而 monitor 是设备或动词。

entries.definition: giving or serving as a warning. It keeps the Latin sense of admonition and is mostly formal.
entries.definitionCN: 给予警告的，或起警告作用的。它保留了拉丁语“告诫”的意思，多用于正式语境。

entries.definition: to warn or reprimand someone firmly but not harshly. It shares the Latin monere root but is a separate verb, not a form of monitor.
entries.definitionCN: 坚定但不严厉地警告或责备某人。它与 monitor 共享拉丁语 monere 词根，但它是另一个动词，不是 monitor 的词形。

entries.definition: a feeling that something is about to happen, especially something bad. It is a warning that comes before the event, built with pre- 'before'.
entries.definitionCN: 一种某事即将发生、尤指坏事的感觉。它是事件之前到来的警告，由 pre-“在前”构成。

entries.definition: to be in charge of people or work and make sure it is done properly. It stresses authority over workers, while monitor stresses continuous checking of signals or conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 负责管理人或工作，确保事情做好。它强调对工作者的权威，而 monitor 强调对信号或状况的持续检查。

entries.definition: to look at something for a period of time, often without measuring it. Monitor usually adds a purpose: to detect change, risk, or poor quality.
entries.definitionCN: 在一段时间内看着某物，通常不进行测量。monitor 通常多一层目的：发现变化、风险或质量问题。

entries.definition: to follow the movement or development of something over time, often by recorded traces. It focuses on where something goes; monitor focuses on whether it stays within limits.
entries.definitionCN: 随时间跟踪某物的移动或发展，常依据记录下来的痕迹。它关注东西去了哪里，monitor 关注它是否仍在限度之内。

entries.definition: to examine people, substances, or signals in order to sort or filter them. It is usually a test applied at a point in time, while monitor is a watch kept over time.
entries.definitionCN: 检查人、物质或信号，以便分类或筛选。它通常是在某一时点施行的检验，而 monitor 是长期保持的观察。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin monere 'warn', the agent noun monitor, and the English family monitoring, monitory, admonish, and premonition.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 monere“警告”、施动名词 monitor，以及英语词族 monitoring、monitory、admonish、premonition。

normal.en: monere means 'to warn, remind'. A monitor is literally 'one who warns' — first a pupil, then an instrument, then a screen.
normal.cn: monere 意为“警告、提醒”。monitor 字面上就是“发出警告的人”——先是学生，再是仪器，最后是屏幕。

normal.en: The school sense is the oldest English one (1540s); the machine and screen senses are centuries later.
normal.cn: 学校职务义是英语里最古老的义项（16 世纪 40 年代）；仪器与屏幕义要晚好几个世纪。

normal.en: The verb arrived in 1924 for checking radio signal quality, which is why 'monitor a channel' still sounds natural.
normal.cn: 动词于 1924 年出现，用于检查无线电信号质量，所以 monitor a channel 至今听起来自然。

normal.en: monitoring is the process, monitory is 'warning', admonish is a separate verb from the same root.
normal.cn: monitoring 是过程，monitory 是“警告的”，admonish 则是同根的另一动词。

normal.en: A monitor differs from a supervisor: it keeps checking a signal or condition, while a supervisor holds authority over people.
normal.cn: monitor 与 supervisor 不同：它持续检查信号或状况，而 supervisor 对人拥有管理权。

abstract.en: Picture a night watchman at a factory gate. He does not repair anything; he looks, checks, and raises the alarm.
abstract.cn: 想象一名守在工厂大门的更夫。他不修理任何东西；他看、检查、发出警报。

abstract.en: Move that watchman into a box on the wall, and he becomes a heart monitor; put his gaze on a screen, and he becomes a display.
abstract.cn: 把这位更夫装进墙上的盒子，他就成了心脏监测仪；把他的目光放到屏幕上，他就成了显示器。

abstract.en: The word always means attention spread over time: a single look is not monitoring, however careful it is.
abstract.cn: 这个词始终表示铺在时间上的注意：只看一眼，无论多仔细，都不算监测。

examples.en: Nurses monitor the patient's pulse and blood pressure every hour.
examples.cn: 护士每小时监测病人的脉搏与血压。

examples.en: The app monitors how much time you spend on each website.
examples.cn: 这个应用监控你在每个网站上花多少时间。

examples.en: The teacher left a monitor in charge of the class while she fetched the keys.
examples.cn: 老师去取钥匙时，让班长负责管班。

dict_mnemonic.text: “莫离他”——莫要离开他，他一直在旁边盯着、随时提醒你 → monitor 监视器；监测（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 monere“警告、提醒”的施动名词 monitor“告诫者”，核心是“持续盯着并随时发出提醒”。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of monitor, all held together by one figure: someone standing beside a thing, watching without stopping and speaking up when something is wrong.
sensesIntro.cn: monitor 的十个义项都由同一个形象串起：有人站在某物旁边，不停地看，一有不对就出声提醒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a warner standing beside, eyes fixed on one spot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个站在旁边、目光钉在一处的告诫者。

branches.en: INSTRUMENTS: the warner becomes a measuring device, and the screen that shows its check takes the same name.
branches.cn: 仪器：告诫者变成测量设备，显示这项检查的屏幕也沿用了同一个名字。

branches.en: PEOPLE: the oldest senses keep a person in the role, either a pupil keeping order or an official who warns.
branches.cn: 人：最古老的义项让一个人留在这个角色里，或是维持秩序的学生，或是提出告诫的官员。

branches.en: WATCHING: the verb checks quantities over time, and when aimed at people it becomes surveillance.
branches.cn: 注视：动词随时间检查数量，而当对象转向人时，它就变成监控。

branches.en: LISTENING: a channel is watched with the ears, the earliest verb use of all.
branches.cn: 监听：频道是用耳朵看的，这是所有动词用法中最早的一个。

branches.en: THE NAME TRAVELS: a lizard fabled to warn, an ironclad built to admonish, and a background program that keeps checking.
branches.cn: 名字远行：传说会预警的蜥蜴、为告诫而造的铁甲舰，以及持续检查的后台程序。

intro.en: Monitor is a Latin agent noun in -itor built on mon- 'warn'. English adds -ing, -y, -ial and -ship, while the same root also reaches English through admonish, monition, and premonition.
intro.cn: monitor 是拉丁语中以 -itor 结尾的施动名词，词干 mon- 意为“警告”。英语加上 -ing、-y、-ial 与 -ship，同一词根还通过 admonish、monition、premonition 进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is monere 'warn, remind', its agent noun monitor, and the action noun monitio 'a warning'. Summon also belongs here: Latin summonere meant 'hint, remind, warn'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词族包括 monere“警告、提醒”、它的施动名词 monitor，以及行为名词 monitio“警告”。summon 也属于这里：拉丁语 summonere 意为“暗示、提醒、警告”。

items.meaning: one who warns or checks; a checking device
items.meaningCN: 告诫者；检查者；监测设备（mon- 警告 + -itor 施动名词）
items.example: The monitor on the wall showed a steady line.
items.exampleCN: 墙上的监测仪显示出一条平稳的线。

items.meaningCN: 监测；监控（-ing 构成过程名词）
items.example: The patient was kept under close monitoring.
items.exampleCN: 病人被置于密切监测之下。

items.meaningCN: 告诫的；警告的（-ory 构成形容词）
items.example: He gave a monitory glance at the noisy table.
items.exampleCN: 他朝吵闹的那桌投去一个警告的目光。

items.meaning: relating to a monitor or prefect
items.meaningCN: 级长的；监督的（-ial 构成形容词）
items.example: The monitorial duties rotated each week.
items.exampleCN: 级长职责每周轮换。

items.meaningCN: 告诫；温和地责备（ad- 向 + mon- 警告）
items.example: The coach admonished the players for arriving late.
items.exampleCN: 教练因球员迟到而告诫了他们。

items.example: She ignored the admonition and drove faster.
items.exampleCN: 她无视那句告诫，反而开得更快。

items.meaning: a warning, especially an official one
items.meaningCN: 警告；正式告诫（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: The court issued a monition to the landowner.
items.exampleCN: 法院向那位土地所有者发出正式警告。

items.meaning: a feeling that something is coming
items.meaningCN: 预感；事前警告（pre- 在前 + monition 警告）
items.example: She had a premonition that the flight would be delayed.
items.exampleCN: 她预感到那趟航班会延误。

items.meaningCN: 召唤；传唤（sum- 暗中 + mon- 提醒）
items.example: The manager summoned the clerk to her office.
items.exampleCN: 经理把那名职员叫到办公室。

items.structure: Greek Mentor, perhaps from PIE *men- 'to think'
items.meaningCN: 导师；可信赖的顾问（同出“思考”词根）
items.example: She became a mentor to the younger researchers.
items.exampleCN: 她成了年轻研究者的导师。

latinEntries.meaning: one who warns, reminds, or checks

definition_zh: 垄断；垄断企业；专卖权；独占
definition_en: exclusive control of a market or commodity by a single seller
core_image: 一条街只有一家店开门，橱窗上贴着唯一的价目表，顾客排成长队也别无选择
scene: 小镇上唯一的一家加油站挂出新的价目牌，排队的车主只能接受。A local monopoly can raise prices until customers travel to a distant substitute.
sceneCN: 这里 monopoly 指「由单一卖方控制的市场结构」（第 1 个义项：市场上只有一个卖方）；句意为地方性垄断可以把价格提高，直到顾客愿意去远处寻找替代品。图中可辨识物件：唯一的加油站、单一价目牌、排队车辆、远处的替代站点。

pos.zh: 垄断；垄断企业；专卖权；独占

senses.title: A market with one seller
senses.definition: a market structure in which a single seller supplies the whole demand and faces no direct rival
senses.definitionCN: 由单一卖方供应全部需求、没有直接对手的市场结构
senses.example: The island's ferry service is a monopoly with no alternative route.
senses.exampleCN: 岛上的渡轮服务是一种没有替代航线的垄断。
senses.why: monos 'single' plus polein 'sell' gives the literal reading: one seller for the whole market.
senses.whyCN: monos「单一」加 polein「卖」给出字面读法：整个市场只有一个卖方。

senses.title: An exclusive right granted by law
senses.definition: a legal privilege allowing one party alone to trade in a good or service
senses.definitionCN: 允许某一方独自经营某种商品或服务的法定特权
senses.example: The old charter gave the company a monopoly on salt.
senses.exampleCN: 旧特许状给了这家公司食盐的专营权。
senses.why: the Greek word first named a concession granted by a city, so the legal sense is older than the economic one.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词最初指城邦授予的特许，因此法律义比经济义更早。

senses.title: The commodity under exclusive control
senses.definition: the good or service that only one supplier is allowed or able to provide
senses.definitionCN: 只允许或只能够由一家供应商提供的商品或服务
senses.example: Broadcasting was once a monopoly of the state.
senses.exampleCN: 广播曾经是国家独占的事业。
senses.why: English allows the word to stand for the thing controlled, not only for the control itself.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许这个词指被控制的对象，而不只是控制本身。

senses.title: The firm that holds the market
senses.definition: the company or organization that enjoys exclusive control
senses.definitionCN: 享有独占控制权的公司或机构
senses.example: Regulators treated the railway as a monopoly and capped its fares.
senses.exampleCN: 监管者把这家铁路公司当作垄断企业，并限制其票价。
senses.why: metonymy turns the structure into the actor, so monopoly can mean the monopolist.
senses.whyCN: 转喻把结构变成行为者，于是 monopoly 可以指垄断企业。

senses.title: A state monopoly
senses.definition: exclusive government control of a trade, often for revenue or public order
senses.definitionCN: 政府对某项贸易的独占控制，常用于增加财政收入或维护公共秩序
senses.example: The tobacco monopoly supplies a large share of the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 烟草专卖提供了预算的很大一部分。
senses.why: early modern states used exclusive grants as a tax-collecting device, and the phrase kept that association.
senses.whyCN: 近代早期国家把专营特许当作征税工具，这个说法保留了这层联系。

senses.title: A temporary monopoly from a patent
senses.titleCN: 专利或版权带来的暂时独占
senses.definition: exclusive commercial use of an invention or work for a limited term
senses.definitionCN: 在有限期限内对某项发明或作品的独占商业使用
senses.example: The patent gave the maker a monopoly for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 专利给了制造商二十年的独占期。
senses.why: intellectual property is a deliberate, time-limited monopoly meant to reward disclosure.
senses.whyCN: 知识产权是一种有意设置、期限有限的垄断，用以奖励公开。

senses.title: A natural monopoly
senses.definition: a market where high fixed costs make one supplier cheaper than several
senses.definitionCN: 固定成本很高、使一家供应比多家供应更便宜的市场
senses.example: Water pipes form a natural monopoly because duplicating them is wasteful.
senses.exampleCN: 水管构成自然垄断，因为重复铺设是浪费。
senses.why: economists call it natural because the single supplier arises from cost structure, not from a legal grant.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家称之为「自然」，因为单一供应来自成本结构，而非法律授予。

senses.title: Exclusive possession of anything
senses.titleCN: 对任何事物的排他性掌控（比喻义）
senses.definition: complete control of a thing or topic so that others have no share
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物或话题的完全控制，使他人无从分享
senses.example: The city does not have a monopoly on good ideas.
senses.exampleCN: 好主意并非这座城市所独占。
senses.why: detached from trade, the word keeps only its core of being the sole holder.
senses.whyCN: 脱离贸易语境后，这个词只保留「唯一持有者」这一核心。

intro.en: Monopoly comes from Greek monopōlion 'exclusive right to sell', built on monos 'alone' and pōlein 'to sell', and enters English through Latin monopolium. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: monopoly 来自希腊 monopōlion「独家售卖权」，由 monos「单独」与 pōlein「卖」构成，经拉丁 monopolium 进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Monos meant 'alone, single'. The same element opens monologue, monorail and monarchy, where it combines with different second terms.
items.cn: monos 意为「单独的、唯一的」。同一成分出现在 monologue、monorail 与 monarchy 的开头，与不同的第二成分组合。

items.en: Pōlein meant 'to sell'. The -poly of monopoly is this verb, not Greek polys 'many', and it has nothing to do with polis 'city'.
items.cn: pōlein 意为「卖」。monopoly 中的 -poly 是这个动词，而非希腊语 polys「多」，也与 polis「城邦」无关。

items.en: Monopōlion named an exclusive sale or a concession granted by a city, especially the right to sell a particular commodity.
items.cn: monopōlion 指独家售卖或城邦授予的特许，尤其是经营某种商品的专权。

items.en: Latin took the Greek noun as monopolium and used it for exclusive trading rights, including grants made by rulers.
items.cn: 拉丁语把希腊名词吸收为 monopolium，用于独家贸易权，包括统治者授予的特许。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the sixteenth century, first for royal grants and later for any single-seller market as economics developed.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入这个词，先指王室特许，随着经济学发展又指任何单一卖方市场。

items.en: The exact first English citation is approximate. The deeper origin of pōlein is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: 最早的英语书证年代只是约数。pōlein 的更深来源属重构形式，并非有直接书证。

note.en: Group one holds neighbouring market structures whose Greek second elements are often confused; group two holds words for control or exclusive dealing that are not market structures.
note.cn: 第一组是第二成分常被混淆的邻近市场结构；第二组是表示控制或独家交易、但并非市场结构的词。

entries.definition: A market with a single buyer; its Greek second element is opsōnein 'to buy', so it is the mirror image of monopoly.
entries.definitionCN: 只有一个买方的市场；其希腊第二成分是 opsōnein「买」，因此是 monopoly 的镜像。

entries.definition: A market dominated by a small number of sellers; the second element is the same verb 'to sell', but the first is oligos 'few'.
entries.definitionCN: 由少数卖方支配的市场；第二成分同为「卖」这个动词，但第一成分是 oligos「少数」。

entries.definition: A market with two dominant sellers, built with Latin duo- on the same Greek selling element.
entries.definitionCN: 由两家主要卖方构成的市场，以拉丁 duo- 接同一个希腊「卖」成分。

entries.definition: The person or firm that holds a monopoly; the structure is monopoly, while the holder is the monopolist.
entries.definitionCN: 持有垄断地位的人或企业；结构是 monopoly，持有者则是 monopolist。

entries.definition: To gain control of a commodity by buying enough of it to dictate price; it is an action, not a market structure.
entries.definitionCN: 通过买下足够多的商品来控制价格；它是一种行为，而非市场结构。

entries.definition: The state of being restricted to one party; a monopoly is one legal or economic form of exclusivity.
entries.definitionCN: 仅限一方享有的状态；垄断是排他性的一种法律或经济形式。

entries.definition: An agreement among independent sellers to fix prices or divide markets; it imitates monopoly without a single seller.
entries.definitionCN: 独立卖方之间固定价格或划分市场的协议；它模仿垄断，却没有单一卖方。

entries.definition: In late nineteenth-century law, a trust was a combination of firms placed under shared trustees, the target of early antitrust law.
entries.definitionCN: 在 19 世纪后期的法律中，trust 指置于共同受托人下的企业联合，是早期反垄断法的对象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: monos 'single' + polein 'sell': one seller for the whole market.
normal.cn: monos「单一」+ polein「卖」：整个市场只有一个卖方。

normal.en: The family runs monopoly, monopolist, monopolize, monopolistic, monopolization.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 monopoly、monopolist、monopolize、monopolistic、monopolization。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the market sense: natural monopoly, state monopoly, monopoly power.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出市场义：自然垄断、国家专卖、垄断力量。

normal.en: The -poly here is 'sell', not 'many': oligopoly and duopoly use the same verb.
normal.cn: 这里的 -poly 是「卖」而非「多」：oligopoly 与 duopoly 用的是同一个动词。

normal.en: Its mirror image is monopsony, where one buyer faces many sellers.
normal.cn: 它的镜像是 monopsony，即一个买方面对许多卖方。

abstract.en: Picture a street with one lit window and a queue outside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街上只有一扇亮着的橱窗，门外排着队。

abstract.en: Picture a single key that opens every door in a building.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙能打开一栋楼里的每一扇门。

abstract.en: Picture one price tag that nobody on the street can undercut.
abstract.cn: 想象一张街上无人能压低的价签。

examples.en: The government broke up the monopoly after a decade of complaints.
examples.cn: 在十年投诉之后，政府拆分了这家垄断企业。

examples.en: A patent is a legal monopoly limited in time and scope.
examples.cn: 专利是一种在时间与范围上受限的法定垄断。

examples.en: No single company should have a monopoly on the public record.
examples.cn: 不应由任何一家公司独占公共记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mono（单一）+ poly（卖）」——整个市场只有一家在卖 → 垄断

root: 希腊 monos「单独」+ pōlein「卖」→ 希腊 monopōlion「独家售卖权」→ 拉丁 monopolium → 英语 monopoly。此处的 -poly 是「卖」，与 polys「多」及 polis「城邦」无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one seller: a single hand holds the whole supply, and that hold is then seen as a market structure, a legal grant, the commodity, the firm, a state trade, a patent term, a cost-driven case, and finally any exclusive possession.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个卖方展开：一只手握住全部供给，这个握有再依次被视为市场结构、法律授予、被控商品、企业本身、国家贸易、专利期限、成本造成的特例，最后是任何排他性占有。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one lit shop window on a street, with a queue that has nowhere else to go.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条街上只有一扇亮着的橱窗，队伍无处可去。

branches.en: STRUCTURE AND ACTOR: the single-seller market, and the firm that occupies it.
branches.cn: 结构与行为者：单一卖方市场，以及占据它的企业。

branches.en: GRANT AND OBJECT: a legal privilege, and the commodity that privilege covers.
branches.cn: 授予与对象：一项法律特权，以及该特权覆盖的商品。

branches.en: THE STATE: the same exclusive hold exercised for revenue or order.
branches.cn: 国家：为财政收入或秩序行使的同一种独占。

branches.en: TIME-LIMITED AND COST-DRIVEN: a patent term, and a market where fixed costs favour one supplier.
branches.cn: 限期与成本驱动：专利期限，以及固定成本偏向单一卖方的市场。

branches.en: ANY EXCLUSIVE HOLD: the word detached from trade and used for ideas or records.
branches.cn: 任何独占：脱离贸易后被用于思想或记录的词。

intro.en: Monopoly is a Greek compound filtered through Latin, so its two Greek elements can be read apart, and English then built a whole family on the noun.
intro.cn: monopoly 是经拉丁语过滤的希腊复合词，因此两个希腊成分可以分开读，英语随后又在这个名词上建起整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin monopolium carries the Greek compound into English; the family then adds -ist, -ize and -ation, while monopsony replaces the selling element with a buying one.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 monopolium 把这个希腊复合词带入英语；词族随后加 -ist、-ize 与 -ation，而 monopsony 把「卖」的成分换成「买」。

items.example: The element also opens monologue and monorail.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分也出现在 monologue 与 monorail 的开头。

items.example: The selling element is shared by oligopoly and duopoly.
items.exampleCN: 这个「卖」的成分由 oligopoly 与 duopoly 共享。

items.example: A local monopoly raised prices without fear.
items.exampleCN: 一家地方垄断者无所顾忌地提价。

items.example: The monopolist owned every pipeline in the valley.
items.exampleCN: 这家垄断企业拥有谷地里的每一条管道。

items.example: The monopolistic pricing drew regulatory attention.
items.exampleCN: 垄断定价引起了监管注意。

items.example: One firm monopolized the supply of spare parts.
items.exampleCN: 一家企业独占了备件供应。

items.example: Monopolization of the route took only three years.
items.exampleCN: 这条航线的垄断化只用了三年。

items.example: A monopsony can push purchase prices down.
items.exampleCN: 买方垄断可以把收购价压低。

items.example: The route is a duopoly of two airlines.
items.exampleCN: 这条航线是两家航空公司的双寡头。

items.example: An oligopoly kept prices stable for years.
items.exampleCN: 寡头格局让价格多年保持稳定。

latinEntries.meaning: a market with a single buyer

definition_zh: 纪念碑的；纪念性的；巨大的；具有重大而持久意义的；（口语）极大的（错误等）
definition_en: serving as a monument; very large or imposing; historically important; extreme in degree
core_image: 游客站在巨大的石门前，门框高得让人显得很小，石缝里长着细草
scene: 游客站在巨大的石门前，人显得很小。The monumental gateway dwarfs every visitor who passes through.
sceneCN: 这里 monumental 指「巨大而宏伟的」（第 2 个义项：体量宏大）；句意为这座宏伟的门楼让每个穿过的人都显得渺小。

pos.zh: 纪念碑的；纪念性的；巨大的；重大的；极端的

derivatives.zh: monumental + -ity（性质后缀）→ 纪念性；宏伟感
monumental + -ly（副词后缀）→ 巨大地；极其
monumental + -ize（动词后缀）→ 使成为纪念物
monumental 去掉 -al → 纪念碑；纪念物

senses.title: Of or serving as a monument
senses.definition: belonging to a monument or serving to commemorate someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 属于纪念碑的，或用于纪念某人某事的
senses.example: The monumental inscription was cut deep enough to survive centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇纪念铭文刻得足够深，得以留存数百年。
senses.why: the adjective simply adds -al to monument, so its first job is to describe memorial objects.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是给 monument 加 -al，因此首要职能是描述纪念物件。

senses.title: Very large and imposing
senses.definition: extremely large, solid or grand in appearance
senses.definitionCN: 在外观上极大、坚固或壮丽
senses.example: The monumental gateway dwarfs every visitor who passes through.
senses.exampleCN: 这座宏伟的门楼让每个穿过的人都显得渺小。
senses.why: memorial buildings were built oversized to impress, so size became part of the adjective's meaning.
senses.whyCN: 纪念建筑常被建得超大以震撼人心，因此「巨大」成为形容词义的一部分。

senses.title: Historically important and enduring
senses.titleCN: 具有重大而持久意义的
senses.definition: of great and lasting importance in history or culture
senses.definitionCN: 在历史或文化上具有重大而持久的重要性
senses.example: The treaty was a monumental step toward peace.
senses.exampleCN: 这项条约是迈向和平的重大一步。
senses.why: what deserves a monument is what a society wants to remember, so importance follows from the memorial core.
senses.whyCN: 值得立碑的东西就是社会想记住的东西，因此「重要」由纪念核心引申而来。

senses.title: Of great artistic or intellectual scale
senses.titleCN: 艺术或思想规模宏大的
senses.definition: large in scope, ambition or intellectual reach, as a work of art or scholarship
senses.definitionCN: 在范围、雄心或思想深度上宏大的，如艺术作品或学术成果
senses.example: The novel is a monumental study of a single family.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说是对一个家族的大规模研究。
senses.why: size moves from stone to thought: a work that covers everything earns the same adjective.
senses.whyCN: 「大」从石头转到思想：包罗万象的作品获得同一个形容词。

senses.title: Extreme, especially a mistake
senses.definition: used informally to mean extremely bad, foolish or costly
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示极坏、极蠢或代价极高
senses.example: Leaving the deed unsigned was a monumental blunder.
senses.exampleCN: 没在契约上签字是极大的失误。
senses.why: a huge mistake looks like a huge stone monument to failure, an ironic use of the size sense.
senses.whyCN: 巨大错误像一座为失败而立的大石碑，是对「巨大」义的反讽用法。

senses.title: Massive in effort or cost
senses.definition: requiring enormous effort, money or time
senses.definitionCN: 需要极大努力、金钱或时间
senses.example: The restoration was a monumental task for a small team.
senses.exampleCN: 对一个小团队来说，这次修复是一项艰巨无比的任务。
senses.why: a task that fills the whole horizon looks as large as a memorial building, so effort borrows the size sense.
senses.whyCN: 占满整个视野的任务看起来像纪念建筑一样大，因此「努力」借用了「体量」义。

senses.title: Commemorative in function
senses.definition: created or used to preserve public memory rather than for daily use
senses.definitionCN: 为保存公共记忆而非日常使用而创造或使用的
senses.example: The arch is monumental in function, not a road building.
senses.exampleCN: 这座拱门在功能上是纪念性的，不是交通建筑。
senses.why: function, not size, decides this sense: the structure exists to be remembered through, not used as a route.
senses.whyCN: 决定这一义的是功能而非大小：这座建筑的存在是为了被记住，而不是当作路线使用。

senses.title: Relating to ancient monuments
senses.definition: connected with the study or preservation of ancient monuments
senses.definitionCN: 与古代纪念物的研究或保护有关的
senses.example: The survey maps every monumental site in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 这次调查标出了山谷中每一处古代纪念遗址。
senses.why: heritage work uses the adjective in its oldest sense, pointing back to the stones themselves.
senses.whyCN: 遗产工作使用这个形容词最古老的义项，指回石头本身。

intro.en: Monumental is monument plus the Latin adjective suffix -alis. The 'very large' sense grew from the oversized scale of memorial buildings, and later spread to achievements and mistakes.
intro.cn: monumental 是 monument 加拉丁形容词后缀 -alis。『巨大』义起源于纪念建筑的超常体量，后来扩展到成就与错误。

items.en: Monumentum meant a memorial or reminder, the noun behind the adjective.
items.cn: monumentum 指纪念物或提醒之物，是形容词背后的名词。

items.en: The suffix -alis meant 'relating to', the regular way to make an adjective from a noun.
items.cn: 后缀 -alis 意为「与……有关的」，是由名词构成形容词的常规方式。

items.en: English formed monumental to mean 'of a monument' or 'serving as a memorial'.
items.cn: 英语构成 monumental，意为「纪念碑的」或「起纪念作用的」。

items.en: Because memorial buildings were deliberately oversized, the adjective acquired the sense 'very large'.
items.cn: 由于纪念建筑刻意造得超大，这个形容词获得了「巨大」的意思。

items.en: In modern use it also describes great achievements, huge tasks and extreme errors.
items.cn: 在现代用法中，它也描述伟大成就、艰巨任务与极端错误。

note.en: Group one holds adjectives of size and grandeur easily confused with monumental; group two holds words for importance.
note.cn: 第一组是容易与 monumental 混淆的表示大小与宏伟的形容词；第二组是表示重要性的词。

entries.definition: The memorial object itself; monumental is the adjective describing it or something huge.
entries.definitionCN: 纪念物件本身；monumental 是描述它或描述巨大事物的形容词。

entries.definition: Of great consequence, often for events; it shares the sound but comes from momentum, not monere.
entries.definitionCN: 后果重大，常用于事件；发音相近，但来自 momentum，而非 monere。

entries.definition: Relating to the basic elements or to raw natural forces; the ending is similar but the root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 与基本元素或原始自然力有关；词尾相似，词根不同。

entries.definition: Serving as a foundation; it shares -mental but comes from fundus, a bottom.
entries.definitionCN: 作为基础的；共享 -mental 词尾，但来自 fundus「底部」。

entries.definition: Extremely large, often with a sense of excess; monumental adds the memorial or historic dimension.
entries.definitionCN: 极大，常带过度意味；monumental 增添了纪念或历史维度。

entries.definition: Large and impressive in appearance or style; it stresses dignity rather than memory.
entries.definitionCN: 外观或风格上宏大而令人印象深刻；强调尊严，而非记忆。

entries.definition: Important in history, often for a single event; monumental stresses lasting commemorative weight.
entries.definitionCN: 历史上重要，常指单一事件；monumental 强调持久的纪念分量。

entries.definition: Very large, heavy and solid; it describes physical bulk, not significance.
entries.definitionCN: 极大、极重且坚实；描述物理体量，而非意义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the reminder noun, the Latin suffix and the real scale of memorial buildings.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：『提醒』名词、拉丁后缀与纪念建筑的真实体量。

normal.en: monument plus -al makes the describing word.
normal.cn: monument 加 -al 构成描述词。

normal.en: Memorial buildings were built oversized to impress, which produced the 'huge' sense.
normal.cn: 纪念建筑被造得超大以震撼人心，由此产生「巨大」义。

normal.en: A monumental achievement is one a culture would put on a plinth.
normal.cn: 不朽成就就是文化愿意放上基座的成就。

normal.en: A monumental error is a huge stone raised to failure.
normal.cn: 极大错误是为失败竖起的一块大石。

normal.en: The adverb monumentally often means simply extremely.
normal.cn: 副词 monumentally 常只表示「极其」。

abstract.en: Monumental is memory measured in tons.
abstract.cn: monumental 是以吨计的记忆。

abstract.en: It is the adjective a building wears when it wants to outlive its city.
abstract.cn: 它是建筑想比城市活得更久时穿上的形容词。

abstract.en: A monumental mistake is a monument no one meant to build.
abstract.cn: 极大的错误是一座没人打算建的纪念碑。

examples.en: The cathedral is a monumental work of medieval engineering.
examples.cn: 这座大教堂是中世纪工程的宏伟作品。

examples.en: They made a monumental effort to finish before winter.
examples.cn: 他们付出巨大努力，要在冬天前完工。

examples.en: The report contained a monumental error in its figures.
examples.cn: 报告的数字里有一个极大的错误。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「monument（纪念碑）+ al」——像纪念碑一样大 → 巨大的、不朽的

root: monument（拉丁 monumentum「纪念物」）+ -al（拉丁形容词后缀 -alis）→ monumental；『巨大』义由纪念建筑的超常体量引申，再扩展到成就与错误。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses grow from memorial function to physical size, then to historic weight, artistic scope, extreme degree, effort, public memory and ancient sites.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从纪念功能长到体量，再到历史分量、艺术规模、极端程度、耗费、公共记忆与古代遗址。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a doorway built so large that a person becomes a small mark at its base.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道造得极大的门，人在门脚变成一个小小的记号。

branches.en: MEMORIAL FUNCTION: describing a monument and acting as one are the same purpose seen as label and as use.
branches.cn: 纪念功能：描述纪念碑与起纪念碑作用，是同一目的在标签与用途两面。

branches.en: GREAT BULK: an oversized gateway and a massive task both measure size in effort or stone.
branches.cn: 巨大体量：超大城门与艰巨任务都以石头或努力衡量大小。

branches.en: WEIGHT OF ACHIEVEMENT: historic importance and grand intellectual scope both make a work worth remembering.
branches.cn: 成就的分量：历史重要性与宏大的思想规模都让作品值得被记住。

branches.en: IRONIC EXTREME: a monumental blunder turns size into blame.
branches.cn: 反讽的极端：极大失误把「大」变成责备。

branches.en: ANCIENT SITES: the adjective returns to old stones in heritage work.
branches.cn: 古代遗址：在遗产工作中，这个形容词又回到古老的石头。

intro.en: Monumental is a regular Latin-derived adjective from monument, and its endings also build abstract nouns and adverbs.
intro.cn: monumental 是由 monument 规则地派生出的拉丁式形容词，其词尾还构成抽象名词与副词。

latinIntro.en: The suffix -alis becomes English -al; -itas becomes -ity in monumentality, and -iter becomes -ly in the adverb.
latinIntro.cn: 后缀 -alis 变成英语 -al；-itas 在 monumentality 中变成 -ity，-iter 在副词中变成 -ly。

items.example: The noun supplies the base.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供基础。

items.example: The suffix makes the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成形容词。

items.example: The gate is monumental.
items.exampleCN: 这座门极为宏伟。

items.example: Monumentality names the quality.
items.exampleCN: monumentality 命名这种性质。

items.example: Monumentally means extremely.
items.exampleCN: monumentally 意为极其。

items.example: To monumentalize is to make into a monument.
items.exampleCN: monumentalize 是使成为纪念物。

items.example: Monumentalization is the process.
items.exampleCN: monumentalization 是这一过程。

items.example: The deepest root still means remind.
items.exampleCN: 最深词根仍表示「提醒」。

monumental + -ly（副词后缀）→ 巨大地；极其
monumental + -ize（动词后缀）→ 使成为纪念物
monumental 去掉 -al → 纪念碑；纪念物

definition_zh: 心情；情绪；气氛；语气（语法）；一时的兴致
definition_en: a temporary state of feeling, or the atmosphere of a place or group, or a grammatical category of the verb
core_image: 天气没有变，屋里的人却觉得整间房子忽明忽暗，像云在屋顶上走
scene: 排练到一半，指挥忽然放下手，说今天先到这里，因为整个乐队已经提不起劲。The conductor stopped the rehearsal because the mood in the hall had gone flat.
sceneCN: 这里 mood 指「一群人当下共同的情绪基调」（第 1 个义项：一时的情绪状态）；句意为指挥中止排练，因为大厅里的情绪已经没了劲。图中可辨识物件：放下的指挥棒、松开的谱架、空着的上半场座位；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 心情；情绪；气氛；语气（语法）
情绪波动；一时的心情变化

senses.title: A temporary state of feeling
senses.definition: the way a person feels at a particular time, seen as passing rather than fixed
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在某段时间里的感受状态，被视为会过去而非固定
senses.example: The conductor stopped the rehearsal because the mood in the hall had gone flat.
senses.exampleCN: 指挥中止排练，因为大厅里的情绪已经没了劲。
senses.why: the oldest English sense is simply 'mind, disposition', so the word names the weather inside a person rather than their climate.
senses.whyCN: 最早的英语义就是「心境、性情」，因此这个词命名的是人内部的天气，而不是气候。

senses.title: The atmosphere of a place
senses.definition: the feeling that a room, a street or a gathering gives off
senses.definitionCN: 一间屋子、一条街或一场聚会所散发出的感受
senses.example: Candles on the tables changed the mood of the whole restaurant.
senses.exampleCN: 桌上的蜡烛改变了整间餐馆的气氛。
senses.why: the same word moves from one head to a space, because a space is read as having a temper of its own.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词从一颗脑袋移到一个空间，因为空间被读作有自己的脾气。

senses.title: A spell of bad temper
senses.definition: a period of sulking or irritability, often named in the plural and with a possessive
senses.definitionCN: 一段闷气或易怒的时期，常以复数并带物主词出现
senses.example: He has been in one of his moods since the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 开会之后他一直闹着脾气。
senses.why: when the passing state is unpleasant, the plural turns it into a recurring event that others learn to expect.
senses.whyCN: 当这种会过去的状态并不愉快时，复数把它变成别人学会预期、一再发生的事。

senses.title: A grammatical category
senses.definition: the form of a verb that shows whether it states, commands or supposes
senses.definitionCN: 动词的形式，表明它是在陈述、命令还是假设
senses.example: English marks the imperative mood by leaving the subject out.
senses.exampleCN: 英语通过省去主语来标记祈使语气。
senses.why: this sense is a different word altogether, borrowed from Latin modus 'measure, manner', and it means a manner of speaking.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项其实是另一个词，借自拉丁 modus「尺度、方式」，意思是说话的方式。

senses.title: The public's temper
senses.definition: the general temper of a group, market or electorate at a given time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时刻一个群体、市场或选民的总体情绪
senses.example: The public mood turned against the plan within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 一周之内公众情绪就转向反对这个方案。
senses.why: one person's weather scaled up becomes a collective climate that politicians claim to read.
senses.whyCN: 一个人的天气放大之后成为集体的气候，政治家声称自己能读出它。

senses.title: Feeling like doing something
senses.definition: the inclination to do a particular thing at a particular moment
senses.definitionCN: 在某个时刻做某件具体事情的倾向
senses.example: She was not in the mood for another long explanation.
senses.exampleCN: 她没有兴致再听一段冗长的解释。
senses.why: the state is now aimed at an object, and 'in the mood for' turns a climate into a door that is either open or shut.
senses.whyCN: 这个状态现在有了对象，「有兴致」把气候变成一扇要么开、要么关的门。

senses.title: Rapid shifts of feeling
senses.definition: quick changes between emotional states, often treated as a symptom or a trait
senses.definitionCN: 情绪状态之间的快速变化，常被当作症状或特质
senses.example: Her mood swings made the household walk on glass.
senses.exampleCN: 她的情绪起落让全家人如履薄冰。
senses.why: the plural measures frequency, turning a state into a pattern that others can chart.
senses.whyCN: 复数衡量的是频率，把一个状态变成旁人能画出来的模式。

senses.title: The key of a work
senses.definition: the prevailing feeling that a painting, film or piece of music is built to produce
senses.definitionCN: 一幅画、一部电影或一段音乐被设计来产生的总体感受
senses.example: The grey palette gives the film a mood of waiting.
senses.exampleCN: 灰调子给这部片子一种等待的基调。
senses.why: artists speak of mood because a work also has weather, and the term lets them tune it deliberately.
senses.whyCN: 艺术家谈基调，是因为作品也有天气，而这个说法让他们能刻意调它。

intro.en: English has two different words written mood. The feeling word is native Old English mod 'mind, courage, temper'. The grammar word was borrowed later from Latin modus 'measure, manner', the same source as mode and model. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 英语里有两个写法相同的 mood。表感受的那个是本族古英语 mod「心、勇气、性情」；语法义的那个则是后来从拉丁 modus「尺度、方式」借入的，与 mode、model 同源。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mod meant 'mind, inner self, courage, anger'. It is Germanic in origin and had no connection with Latin at all.
items.cn: mod 意为「心、内在自我、勇气、愤怒」。它源出日耳曼语，与拉丁语毫无关联。

items.en: As the older senses faded, the word narrowed to a passing state of feeling, the sense it carries today.
items.cn: 随着较早的义项淡出，这个词收窄为一种会过去的感受状态，也就是今天的义项。

items.en: Modus meant 'measure, standard, manner'. Grammarians used it for the manner in which a verb states or commands, and that use entered English.
items.cn: modus 意为「尺度、标准、方式」。语法学家用它指动词陈述或命令的方式，这一用法进入了英语。

items.en: The spelling fell together in Middle English, so that one shape now carries two unrelated histories, one Germanic and one Latin.
items.cn: 两个词在中古英语里拼写合流，于是一个字形现在背着两段互不相关的历史，一段日耳曼，一段拉丁。

items.en: From the eighteenth century the feeling word was extended to rooms, crowds, markets and works of art, and mood music followed in the twentieth.
items.cn: 从 18 世纪起，表感受的那个词被延伸到屋子、人群、市场与艺术品，20 世纪又有了「氛围音乐」。

items.en: Source uncertain: the earliest written forms of the Germanic word are attested but its deeper pre-Germanic origin is a reconstruction, and no first date is agreed for the grammar borrowing.
items.cn: 来源不确定：那个日耳曼词的最早书写形式有书证，但它在日耳曼语之前的更深来源属重构形式；语法义借入的确切年代也没有公认结论。

note.en: Group one holds the word that looks the same but has another history; group two holds feeling words that differ in duration and cause.
note.cn: 第一组是字形相同而历史不同的词；第二组是持续时间与起因不同的感受词。

entries.definition: From Latin modus 'measure, manner': a way of doing something. It looks close to mood but shares history only with the grammar sense.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 modus「尺度、方式」：做事的方式。字形近 mood，但只与语法义共享历史。

entries.definition: Built on the feeling sense: given to sudden low or irritable states.
entries.definitionCN: 由表感受的义项构成：容易陷入突然的低落或烦躁。

entries.definition: Also from modus through a small form meaning 'little measure'; it belongs to design, not to feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 同样出自 modus，经由一个意为「小尺度」的形式；属设计领域，与感受无关。

entries.definition: From the same idea of measure: kept within limits. Nothing of it survives in the feeling word.
entries.definitionCN: 同出「尺度」这一观念：保持在限度之内。表感受的那个词里没有留下它的痕迹。

entries.definition: A distinct surge such as fear or joy; a mood is the longer weather that such surges happen inside.
entries.definitionCN: 如恐惧或喜悦那样一次明确的涌动；mood 是这些涌动所发生的更长的天气。

entries.definition: A settled tendency to become angry, closer to temperament than to a passing state.
entries.definitionCN: 易怒的固定倾向，更接近气质而非一时的状态。

entries.definition: The feel of a space or occasion; it covers the place sense but never the inner state of one person.
entries.definitionCN: 指空间或场合的感受；覆盖「地点」义，却从不指单个人的内在状态。

entries.definition: A plural word for how high or low someone's cheer is, as in high spirits; it measures level, not colour.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个人兴致高低的复数说法，如兴致高；衡量的是水位，而不是颜色。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The feeling sense is native Old English, while the grammar sense came from Latin modus, so one spelling hides two families.
normal.cn: 感受义是本族古英语，语法义则来自拉丁 modus，因此一个拼写藏着两个词族。

normal.en: The family runs mood, moody, moodily, moodiness, mood-altering, mood board.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 mood、moody、moodily、moodiness、mood-altering、mood board。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: in a good mood, in the mood for, mood swings, set the mood.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：心情好、有兴致、情绪波动、定下气氛。

normal.en: Grammar keeps the Latin side alive in phrases like the imperative mood.
normal.cn: 语法在「祈使语气」一类说法里让拉丁那一面活着。

normal.en: Markets and newspapers speak of the public mood, extending one person's weather to a whole country.
normal.cn: 市场与报纸谈「公众情绪」，把一个人的天气扩到整个国家。

abstract.en: Picture a room where the lamp does not change but the walls seem to brighten and dim.
abstract.cn: 想象灯没有变，墙面却似乎忽明忽暗的屋子。

abstract.en: Picture a thermostat that responds to conversation rather than to air.
abstract.cn: 想象一个对谈话而不是对空气作出反应的恒温器。

abstract.en: Picture a door that opens only when the person inside feels like it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇只有在里面的人有兴致时才开的门。

examples.en: The mood in the office lifted as soon as the results arrived.
examples.cn: 结果一到，办公室里的气氛就轻松起来。

examples.en: I am not in the mood for a debate tonight.
examples.cn: 我今晚没兴致辩论。

examples.en: The subjunctive mood is rare in modern spoken English.
examples.cn: 虚拟语气在现代英语口语中很少见。

dict_mnemonic.text: mood 读如「木的」——人一时像木头一样闷着 → 心情、情绪、气氛

root: 两条独立来源：表感受的义项出自古英语 mod「心、勇气、性情」，属日耳曼语；表语气的语法义借自拉丁 modus「尺度、方式」，与 mode、model 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a person has weather, and that weather is then read as a room's temper, as a recurring bad spell, as a manner of speaking, as a public climate, as an open door, as a pattern of swings and finally as a key chosen by an artist.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个动作展开：人有天气，这天气依次被读作一间屋子的脾气、一再出现的坏脾气、一种说话方式、公众气候、一扇开着的门、一串起落的模式，最后是艺术家选定的调子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a room whose lamp never changes, yet the walls seem to brighten and dim as clouds cross the roof.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯始终没变的屋子，云从屋顶走过时墙面却忽明忽暗。

branches.en: WEATHER AND ITS RECORD: one sense is a single stretch of feeling, the other the chart of how often it turns.
branches.cn: 天气与它的记录：一个是单段感受，另一个是它翻转频率的图表。

branches.en: A SPACE WITH A TEMPER: the same weather either fills a room or is deliberately composed into a work.
branches.cn: 有脾气的空间：同一种天气要么充满一间屋子，要么被刻意编进一件作品。

branches.en: THE SPELL OTHERS LEARN: a bad mood made plural becomes a recurring event in a household.
branches.cn: 旁人学会的那阵子：坏心情一旦用复数，就成了一户人家反复发生的事。

branches.en: THE OTHER HISTORY: here the word does not mean feeling at all, but the manner in which a verb speaks.
branches.cn: 另一段历史：这里这个词完全不指感受，而指动词说话的方式。

branches.en: CLIMATE AND INCLINATION: one is a whole public's weather, the other a single door that is open or shut.
branches.cn: 气候与意愿：一个是整个公众的天气，另一个是单扇开或关的门。

intro.en: The word is short and native, so the interesting structure lies in its family and in the separate Latin homograph.
intro.cn: 这个词又短又是本族语，因此有意思的结构在它的词族，以及那个同形异源的拉丁词上。

latinIntro.en: Only the grammar sense has Latin behind it, from modus 'measure, manner'; the feeling word has no Latin ancestry at all.
latinIntro.cn: 只有语法义背后有拉丁语，出自 modus「尺度、方式」；表感受的那个词完全没有拉丁来历。

items.example: The mood in the hall went flat.
items.exampleCN: 大厅里的情绪没了劲。

items.example: It forms the adjective for someone given to moods.
items.exampleCN: 它构成形容某人容易闹情绪的形容词。

items.meaning: given to low or irritable states
items.meaningCN: 容易陷入低落或烦躁的
items.example: He grew moody before exams.
items.exampleCN: 考试前他变得闷闷不乐。

items.example: It turns the adjective into a name for the trait.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成该特质的名称。

items.meaning: the trait of changing mood quickly
items.example: Moodiness is common in adolescence.
items.exampleCN: 情绪多变在青春期很常见。

items.meaning: music chosen to create an atmosphere
items.meaningCN: 为营造气氛而选的音乐
items.example: The café plays mood music all afternoon.
items.exampleCN: 这家咖啡馆整个下午放着氛围音乐。

items.example: The doctor asked about mood swings.
items.exampleCN: 医生询问了情绪波动的情况。

items.structure: Latin modus (source of the grammar sense)
items.example: The grammar sense is a separate Latin borrowing.
items.exampleCN: 语法义是一次独立的拉丁借入。

definition_zh: 道德的；有道德的；寓意；道德准则
definition_en: concerned with right and wrong conduct, good in behaviour, and also the lesson drawn from a story or a set of principles
core_image: 心里那把量是非的尺子
scene: 篝火旁的寓言讲完，孩子们等着大人说出最后那句话。The fable ends with a simple moral about patience.
sceneCN: 这里是「寓意、教训」（第 3 个义项：故事传达的道理）；句意为这则寓言以一句关于耐心的浅显道理收尾。图中可辨识物件：篝火、故事书、围坐的孩子。

derivatives.zh: 由 moral 加 -ity 构成，义为「道德；道德体系」
由 moral 加 -ist 构成，义为「道德主义者；说教者」
由 moral 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「说教；从道德上解释」
由前缀 de-（去掉）加 moralize 构成，义为「使士气低落」

senses.title: Concerned with right and wrong
senses.definition: relating to principles of right and wrong behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 与行为对错的准则有关的
senses.example: Most people share a basic sense of moral duty.
senses.exampleCN: 多数人对道义责任有一种基本的感受。
senses.why: The Latin stem mor- named custom, and custom is exactly where a community's sense of right and wrong is stored.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词干 mor- 本指习俗，而一个群体对是非的判断正存放在习俗里。

senses.title: Good in behaviour
senses.definition: acting in a way that is considered good and honest
senses.definitionCN: 以被认为是善良诚实的方式行事
senses.example: He led a moral life and never cheated anyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他过着品行端正的生活，从不欺骗任何人。
senses.why: If custom supplies the standard, a person who follows it closely can be called moral, so the adjective moves from the rule to the person.
senses.whyCN: 既然习俗提供了标准，紧守标准的人就可以被称为有道德，于是形容词从规则转到了人身上。

senses.title: The lesson of a story
senses.definition: the point or lesson that a story or event is meant to teach
senses.definitionCN: 故事或事件想要教给人的要点或教训
senses.example: The moral of the story is that patience pays.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事的寓意是耐心会有回报。
senses.why: Fables were used to teach conduct, so the adjective's subject matter became a noun for the teaching itself.
senses.whyCN: 寓言本来是用来教人行为的，于是这个形容词所谈的内容就变成名词，指那番教导本身。

senses.title: Principles held by a person or group
senses.definition: the set of principles about right and wrong that someone or a group holds
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某群体所持的一套关于是非的原则
senses.example: She questioned the morals of the people around her.
senses.exampleCN: 她质疑身边那些人的道德准则。
senses.why: Customs can be counted one by one, so the plural names the separate rules a person carries.
senses.whyCN: 习俗可以一条一条地数，于是复数就指一个人所持有的那些具体准则。

intro.en: The word travels from a Latin noun for custom through Cicero's coinage and French into an English word for conduct and for the point of a story.
intro.cn: 这个词从拉丁语表示习俗的名词出发，经西塞罗的造词与法语，进入英语，用来指品行，也指故事的要点。

items.en: Latin mos, whose stem is mor-, meant custom or habitual manner, the unwritten rules a community lived by.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mos 的词干是 mor-，意为习俗或习惯做法，即一个群体赖以生活的成文之外的规矩。

items.en: Cicero is generally credited with coining moralis to render Greek ethikos, giving Latin a word for what concerns character and conduct.
items.cn: 一般认为 moralis 是西塞罗为翻译希腊语 ethikos 而造的，给拉丁语添了一个表示品行与行为的词。

items.en: Old French moral carried the adjective into everyday use for behaviour judged good or bad.
items.cn: 古法语 moral 把这个形容词带入日常使用，用来评判行为的好坏。

items.en: Middle English moral added the noun sense of a lesson drawn from a story, especially in fables.
items.cn: 中古英语的 moral 增加了名词义，指从故事、尤其是寓言中引出的教训。

items.en: Modern English moral works as an adjective for conduct and as a noun for the point of a tale or a set of principles.
items.cn: 现代英语的 moral 既是描述行为的形容词，也是指故事要点或一套原则的名词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same custom stem, while the near-meaning group collects adjectives of good conduct.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「习俗」词干上的词，近义组收描述良好品行的形容词。

entries.definition: The quality of being moral, or a system of moral rules.
entries.definitionCN: 由 moral 加 -ity 构成，义为「道德；道德体系」。

entries.definition: A person who teaches or studies moral rules.
entries.definitionCN: 讲授或研究道德准则的人。

entries.definition: The spirit and confidence of a group, from the same French stem but with a different sense.
entries.definitionCN: 一个群体的士气，同出法语词干但含义不同。

entries.definition: To take away someone's confidence or spirit.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人失去信心或士气。

entries.definition: Following accepted principles of right conduct.
entries.definitionCN: 遵循公认的正当行为原则的。

entries.definition: Showing high moral standards in behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 行为上体现高尚道德的。

entries.definition: Respectable and morally acceptable.
entries.definitionCN: 正派而合乎道德的。

entries.definition: Honest and morally correct in conduct.
entries.definitionCN: 为人诚实、行为端正的。

normalIntro.en: The family grows from a Latin noun for custom, and each branch keeps turning custom into a judgement about conduct.
normalIntro.cn: 这一族词从一个表示习俗的拉丁名词长出来，每个分支都把习俗变成对行为的评判。

normal.en: Latin mos, stem mor-, meant custom, so moral first described the customs a community shared.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mos 的词干是 mor-，意为习俗，所以 moral 最初描述一个群体共享的习俗。

normal.en: Cicero coined moralis for Greek ethikos, linking the word to character rather than to law.
normal.cn: 西塞罗为希腊语 ethikos 造出 moralis，把这个词与品行而非法律联系起来。

normal.en: morality adds -ity to moral: the quality of being concerned with right and wrong.
normal.cn: morality 在 moral 后加 -ity，指与是非有关的性质。

normal.en: The plural morals names the principles a person holds.
normal.cn: 复数的 morals 指一个人所持有的那些原则。

normal.en: The prefix de- in demoralize strips away the spirit that the stem once protected.
normal.cn: demoralize 里的前缀 de- 把词干曾经守护的那股气去掉。

abstract.en: A moral is a line drawn in the sand, and the point of a story is where the line sits.
abstract.cn: 道德是一条划在沙上的线，而故事的要点就是这条线画在哪里。

abstract.en: Customs harden into morals when a community stops asking why.
abstract.cn: 当一个群体不再追问为什么，习俗就凝固成道德。

abstract.en: The same stem gives morale, which shows how a shared mood and a shared code grow from one root.
abstract.cn: 同一词干还给出 morale，说明共同的士气与共同的准则如何从一条根上长出。

examples.en: Most people share a basic sense of moral duty.
examples.cn: 多数人对道义责任有一种基本的感受。

examples.en: The moral of the story is that patience pays.
examples.cn: 这个故事的寓意是耐心会有回报。

examples.en: She questioned the morals of the people around her.
examples.cn: 她质疑身边那些人的道德准则。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莫乱」——莫乱来，凡事讲道德；记住 moral 是道德的。

root: 拉丁语 mos（习俗、风气，词干 mor-）派生出 moralis，意为与品行有关的，经古法语 moral 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the standard drawn from custom; the senses then divide into good conduct itself, the lesson of a tale, and the countable rules a person holds.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是从习俗中画出的标准；义项由此分出端正的品行本身、故事的教训，以及一个人可数的那些准则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler held up against a person's conduct, marking what is allowed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把尺子举在一个人的行为前面，标出哪些是被允许的。

branches.en: a ruler laid across a decision
branches.cn: 一把尺子横在决定之上

branches.en: a person whose conduct never needs explaining
branches.cn: 一个行为从不需要解释的人

branches.en: the last line of a fable
branches.cn: 寓言结尾的那一句话

branches.en: a list of rules a family keeps
branches.cn: 一个家庭守着的一串规矩

branches.en: a tale that teaches a duty
branches.cn: 一则教人尽责的故事

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin noun for custom, a Latin adjective built from it, and two English endings that name its quality and its defenders.
intro.cn: 这个词依托一个表示习俗的拉丁名词、由它构成的拉丁形容词，以及两个分别指「性质」与「维护者」的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun mos and its derived moralis are the direct source of this whole English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 mos 及其派生的 moralis 是这一整族英语词的直接来源。
