definition_zh: 形态学；形态；词法；地貌形态；组织结构
definition_en: the study of the form and structure of organisms, words, or other systems
core_image: 一张工作台上并排摆着骨骼、词卡与地形图，三样东西都在讲同一个问题：它们是什么形状
scene: 在大学的分类学课堂上，教授写下三个问题后说：Morphology alone cannot tell us how two species behave.
sceneCN: 这里 morphology 指「对生物形态的研究」（第 1 个义项：研究生物外形与结构的学科）；句意是单靠形态学无法告诉我们两个物种如何活动。

senses.title: The biological study of form
senses.definition: the branch of biology that studies the form and structure of organisms
senses.definitionCN: 研究生物外形与结构的生物学分支
senses.example: Morphology alone cannot tell us how two species behave.
senses.exampleCN: 单靠形态学无法告诉我们两个物种如何活动。
senses.why: Morphē is form and -logia is study, so the noun names a discipline before it names any particular shape.
senses.whyCN: morphē 是「形状」，-logia 是「研究」，因此这个名词先指一门学科，而非某个具体形状。

senses.title: The form itself, apart from its study
senses.titleCN: 形态本身（而非对其研究）
senses.definition: the actual form and structure of an organism or object
senses.definitionCN: 生物或物体的实际外形与结构
senses.example: The morphology of the shell suggests a burrowing animal.
senses.exampleCN: 贝壳的形态提示这是一种穴居动物。
senses.why: The same noun can metonymically name the object of study, so morphology means the shape as well as the science of shape.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词可以用转喻指研究对象，因此 morphology 既指学科，也指形状本身。

senses.title: The study of word structure
senses.titleCN: 研究词的内部结构的学问
senses.definition: the branch of linguistics that studies how words are built from morphemes
senses.definitionCN: 研究词如何由语素构成的语言学分支
senses.example: English morphology explains why the plural ending changes shape.
senses.exampleCN: 英语词法解释了复数词尾为何改变形式。
senses.why: Linguists took the Greek form word for the internal shape of words, the arrangement of roots and affixes.
senses.whyCN: 语言学家借用了这个希腊「形状」词，指词的内部形状，即词根与词缀的排列。

senses.title: The shape of landforms
senses.definition: the form and development of landforms, studied in geomorphology
senses.definitionCN: 地貌的形状与发育，在地貌学中研究
senses.example: The morphology of the valley records repeated glacial advances.
senses.exampleCN: 山谷的形态记录了多次冰川推进。
senses.why: Earth science borrowed the word for the surface shapes of the planet, which are read as a history of process.
senses.whyCN: 地球科学借用这个词指地表的形状，这些形状被当作过程史来读。

senses.title: The shape of a galaxy
senses.definition: the structural classification of galaxies by their shape
senses.definitionCN: 按形状对星系所作的结构分类
senses.example: Galaxy morphology divides spirals, ellipticals and irregulars.
senses.exampleCN: 星系形态学把星系分为旋涡、椭圆与不规则三类。
senses.why: At great distance only shape survives as evidence, so astronomy makes morphology a classification tool.
senses.whyCN: 在极远的距离上，只有形状还能作为证据，因此天文学把形态学当作分类工具。

senses.title: Microstructure of a material
senses.definition: the internal structure of a material, such as grains and phases
senses.definitionCN: 材料的内部结构，如晶粒与相
senses.example: Heat treatment changed the morphology of the alloy.
senses.exampleCN: 热处理改变了这种合金的组织形态。
senses.why: Materials science applies the word to structures seen under a microscope, where shape controls strength.
senses.whyCN: 材料科学把这个词用于显微镜下所见的结构，那里的形状决定强度。

senses.title: Mathematical morphology
senses.definition: a branch of image analysis that studies shapes with set operations
senses.definitionCN: 用集合运算研究形状的图像分析分支
senses.example: Mathematical morphology removes noise by shrinking and expanding shapes.
senses.exampleCN: 数学形态学通过收缩与扩张形状来去除噪声。
senses.why: Here morphology is literal again: algorithms act on the shape of regions in an image.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 morphology 又回到字面义：算法作用于图像中区域的形状。

senses.title: The form of a city or institution
senses.definition: the spatial or organizational form of a settlement or system
senses.definitionCN: 聚落或系统的空间或组织形态
senses.example: Urban morphology maps streets, plots and building types together.
senses.exampleCN: 城市形态学把街道、地块与建筑类型放在一起绘制。
senses.why: Once form is the object, any organized layout can have a morphology, from streets to institutions.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「形式」成为对象，任何有组织的布局都可以有形态，从街道到机构。

intro.en: Morphology is Greek morphē form plus -logia study, mediated by modern Latin morphologia; the origin of morphē itself is unresolved.
intro.cn: morphology 是希腊 morphē「形状」加 -logia「研究」，经近代拉丁 morphologia 中介；morphē 本身的来源尚无定论。

items.en: Morphē meant form or outward appearance; its deeper origin is uncertain, and a link to meros part is only a hypothesis.
items.cn: morphē 意为形状或外观；其更深来源不确定，与 meros「部分」的联系只是假说。

items.en: Logia, from logos word or account, named a field of study when attached to a root.
items.cn: logia 出自 logos「言词、论述」，接在词根后便指一门研究领域。

items.en: Modern Latin morphologia assembled the two Greek pieces for the study of biological form.
items.cn: 近代拉丁 morphologia 把两个希腊部件组装起来，指对生物形态的研究。

items.en: Nineteenth-century German and French biologists and linguists established morphology as a named science in both fields.
items.cn: 19 世纪德国与法国的生物学家和语言学家使 morphology 在这两个领域都成为有名称的学科。

items.en: Source uncertain as to the root: Greek morphē has no established pre-Greek origin, so any reconstructed Indo-European base is a reconstruction; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根存疑）：希腊 morphē 没有已证实的希腊语之前来源，凡给出的印欧语基形式均属重构形式；英语首见年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same form root; group two holds neighbouring disciplines that also describe structure.
note.cn: 第一组是同一「形状」词根构成的词；第二组是同样描述结构的相邻学科。

entries.definition: The adjective of morphology, used when a noun is needed for a trait or feature.
entries.definitionCN: morphology 的形容词，用于修饰性状或特征。

entries.definition: The smallest meaningful unit of a word; it is what morphology studies, not the study itself.
entries.definitionCN: 词的最小意义单位；它是形态学研究的对象，而非学科本身。

entries.definition: Without definite form, built from the same morphē root with a negative prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 没有确定形状，由同一 morphē 词根加否定前缀构成。

entries.definition: A complete change of form; the root is shared, but the meaning is transformation rather than study.
entries.definitionCN: 形态的彻底改变；共享词根，但意义是转变而非研究。

entries.definition: The study of body parts by dissection; it overlaps with morphology but stresses internal organization.
entries.definitionCN: 通过解剖研究身体各部分的学问；与形态学重叠，但强调内部组织。

entries.definition: The study of how body parts work; it is the functional counterpart of morphology.
entries.definitionCN: 研究身体各部位如何运作的学问；是形态学的功能对应面。

entries.definition: The science of grouping and naming organisms; morphology supplies much of its evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 对生物分组与命名的科学；形态学为其提供大量证据。

entries.definition: The arrangement of parts; morphology is the systematic study of that arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 部件的排列；形态学是对这种排列的系统研究。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Morphē form plus -logia study: the study of shape wherever shape matters.
normal.cn: morphē「形状」加 -logia「研究」：在形状重要的地方研究形状。

normal.en: The family runs morphology, morphological, morphologically, morphologist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 morphology、morphological、morphologically、morphologist。

normal.en: The same noun covers organisms, words and cities.
normal.cn: 同一个名词覆盖生物、词与城市。

normal.en: Biology pairs morphology with physiology: form beside function.
normal.cn: 生物学把形态学与生理学配对：形式与功能并列。

normal.en: Galaxy morphology is a classification, not a laboratory study.
normal.cn: 星系形态学是一种分类，而非实验室研究。

abstract.en: Picture a workbench holding a bone, a word card and a map, all answering one question about shape.
abstract.cn: 想象一张工作台，上面放着骨头、词卡和地图，都在回答同一个关于形状的问题。

abstract.en: Picture a city seen from above as a sentence written in streets.
abstract.cn: 想象从高处看一座城市，街道写成了一句话。

abstract.en: Picture a metal grain enlarged until its outline becomes a landscape.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒金属被放大，轮廓变成一片地貌。

examples.en: Her research combines morphology with molecular phylogeny.
examples.cn: 她的研究把形态学与分子系统发生学结合起来。

examples.en: The morphology of the leaf separates the two varieties.
examples.cn: 叶片的形态把这两个变种区分开来。

examples.en: Urban morphology studies how plots and streets evolve together.
examples.cn: 城市形态学研究地块与街道如何一起演变。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「morph 形状 + ology 学科」——研究形状与结构的学问 → 形态学、词法

root: 希腊 morphē「形状」+ -logia「研究」（出自 logos「言说、论述」），经近代拉丁 morphologia；morphē 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses show one discipline spreading across organisms, words, landforms, galaxies, materials, images and cities, while the core question stays the same: what is the shape.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项显示同一门学问铺展到生物、词、地貌、星系、材料、图像与城市，而核心问题始终不变：形状是什么。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bench where a bone, a word card and a map are examined for the same property, their shape.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张工作台上放着骨头、词卡与地图，被检查的是同一个属性——形状。

branches.en: DISCIPLINE AND OBJECT: morphology is both the study of form and the form being studied.
branches.cn: 学科与对象：形态学既是研究形式的学问，也是被研究的形式本身。

branches.en: WORD SHAPE: roots and affixes are the anatomy of a word.
branches.cn: 词的形状：词根与词缀就是词的解剖结构。

branches.en: LAND AND SKY: the same word describes river terraces and spiral galaxies.
branches.cn: 大地与天空：同一个词描述河流阶地与旋涡星系。

branches.en: MICRO AND ALGORITHM: grains under a microscope and shapes inside an image are read the same way.
branches.cn: 微观与算法：显微镜下的晶粒与图像里的形状用同一种方式读取。

branches.en: ORGANIZED SPACE: a city or an institution can be studied as a form.
branches.cn: 有组织的空间：城市或机构可以作为形式来研究。

intro.en: Morphology is a two-part Greek compound, and each part recurs in a large technical vocabulary shared by biology, linguistics and medicine.
intro.cn: morphology 是一个两部分希腊复合词，每个部分都重现于生物学、语言学与医学共用的技术词汇中。

latinIntro.en: Greek morphē gives the form root; Greek logos gives -logia, the suffix of disciplines from biology to sociology.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 morphē 给出「形状」词根；希腊 logos 给出 -logia，即从生物学到社会学的学科后缀。

items.example: The root names shape across many fields.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根在多个领域指形状。

items.example: The suffix names a discipline.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名一门学科。

items.example: Morphology describes the form of organisms.
items.exampleCN: 形态学描述生物的形态。

items.example: Morphological data supported the split.
items.exampleCN: 形态数据支持这一划分。

items.example: The morphologist measured the shells.
items.exampleCN: 形态学家测量了贝壳。

items.example: Each ending is a morpheme.
items.exampleCN: 每个词尾都是一个语素。

items.example: The glass is amorphous.
items.exampleCN: 玻璃是无定形的。

items.example: The larva undergoes metamorphosis.
items.exampleCN: 幼虫经历变态。

items.example: Geomorphology explains the valley.
items.exampleCN: 地貌学解释了这条山谷。

definition_zh: 马赛克；镶嵌画；镶嵌工艺；拼合而成的整体
definition_en: a picture or pattern made by fixing small coloured pieces into a surface
core_image: 碎成百片的彩石被一块块嵌进灰泥，远看合成一幅完整图画
scene: 考古队在教堂地面清理出一幅由几千块小石子拼成的鸟形图案。The team uncovered a mosaic of tiny stones forming a bird on the church floor.
sceneCN: 这里指「用小石片拼成的镶嵌图案」（第 1 个义项：由许多小块材料嵌成的画面）；句意为考古队在教堂地面清理出一幅小石子拼成的鸟形镶嵌画。可辨识物件：小石片、灰泥、鸟形、刷子、标尺。

pos.zh: 镶嵌式的；由许多小块拼成的

derivatives.zh: 镶嵌艺术家；马赛克工匠（由基础词加表示「从事者」的后缀构成，语义收窄为职业身份）
用镶嵌法装饰的；镶成马赛克图案的（由基础词加表示「被施以……」的后缀构成，语义偏移为状态）
类似镶嵌画的；由细碎单元拼成的（由基础词加表示「像……的」后缀构成，语义偏移为性质描述）

senses.title: Picture made of small pieces
senses.definition: a picture or decorative pattern made by fixing small pieces of stone, glass or tile into a surface
senses.definitionCN: 把小块石头、玻璃或瓷砖嵌进表面而拼成的画面或装饰图案
senses.example: The team uncovered a mosaic of tiny stones forming a bird.
senses.exampleCN: 考古队清理出一幅由小石子拼成鸟形的镶嵌画。
senses.why: The word names the work first. A mosaic exists only because many separate pieces are set side by side, so the picture is literally made of parts.
senses.whyCN: 这个词首先指成品。镶嵌画之所以存在，只因为许多分离的小块被并排嵌在一起，所以画面真的由碎片构成。

senses.title: The art of setting tesserae
senses.titleCN: 镶嵌工艺：把小块材料嵌进表面的手艺
senses.definition: the craft or technique of assembling small pieces into a surface design
senses.definitionCN: 把小块材料拼嵌成表面图案的手艺或技法
senses.example: She studied mosaic in Ravenna for three summers.
senses.exampleCN: 她连续三个夏天在拉文纳学习镶嵌工艺。
senses.why: Once the product was familiar, the name moved to the skill that makes it. The art is defined by the setting of separate pieces, not by any one material.
senses.whyCN: 成品为人熟知之后，名称就转指制作它的技艺。这门艺术的关键是把分离的小块嵌起来，而不在于某一种材料。

senses.title: A floor or wall work
senses.definition: a decorated floor, wall or vault executed in this technique
senses.definitionCN: 用这种技法做成的地面、墙面或拱顶装饰
senses.example: The baptistery ceiling is a gold mosaic of the saints.
senses.exampleCN: 洗礼堂的穹顶是一幅金底圣徒镶嵌画。
senses.why: Mosaic art lives on architecture. Because the pieces are fixed into mortar, the work belongs to the building rather than to a frame.
senses.whyCN: 镶嵌艺术依附于建筑。因为小块被嵌进灰泥，作品属于建筑本身，而不属于画框。

senses.title: A mixture of distinct elements
senses.titleCN: 由不同成分拼合的整体
senses.definition: a whole made of many different elements that remain individually visible
senses.definitionCN: 由许多不同成分构成、各成分仍各自可见的整体
senses.example: The city is a mosaic of languages and cuisines.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市是语言与饮食的拼合体。
senses.why: The visual sense becomes social: separate communities lie side by side like stones in a floor, making one picture without melting into one colour.
senses.whyCN: 视觉义转向社会：不同的群体像地面的石子那样并排相邻，合成一幅图，却没有熔成同一种颜色。

senses.title: Mixed cell populations in genetics
senses.titleCN: 遗传学中由不同细胞群构成的个体
senses.definition: in genetics, an organism or tissue containing cells with more than one genotype
senses.definitionCN: 遗传学中，体内含有一种以上基因型细胞的生物体或组织
senses.example: The lab detected a mosaic in the patient's skin cells.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室在患者的皮肤细胞中检测到嵌合现象。
senses.why: Geneticists borrowed the image of pieces from different sources lying in one body. The whole is one organism, but its cells are not all the same.
senses.whyCN: 遗传学家借用「不同来源的小块同处一体」的意象：整体是一个生物体，细胞却并不完全相同。

senses.title: Image built from many photographs
senses.titleCN: 由许多照片拼成的数字图像
senses.definition: a digital image assembled from many small photographs so that they form a larger picture
senses.definitionCN: 由许多小照片拼合、在远处构成更大画面的数字图像
senses.example: The poster was a mosaic of thousands of reader photos.
senses.exampleCN: 那张海报由数千张读者照片拼成。
senses.why: The digital version repeats the old rule: each tile is a whole image by itself, yet at a distance it becomes one pixel in a larger face.
senses.whyCN: 数字版本重复了旧规则：每一小块本身都是一张完整照片，远看却成为更大画面里的一个像素。

senses.title: Patchwork of habitats in ecology
senses.titleCN: 生态学中由多种生境拼成的格局
senses.definition: in ecology, a landscape made of distinct habitat patches lying side by side
senses.definitionCN: 生态学中，由彼此相邻的不同生境斑块构成的景观
senses.example: Fire created a mosaic of open grass and young forest.
senses.exampleCN: 火灾造成了草地与幼林交错的生境格局。
senses.why: Ecologists see a landscape as a floor of patches. Each patch keeps its own character, and the whole supports more life than any single patch would.
senses.whyCN: 生态学家把景观看成由斑块铺成的地面。每块保留自己的性质，整体能供养的生命比任何单块都多。

senses.title: Made of many small parts
senses.titleCN: 形容词义：由许多小部分构成的
senses.definition: made up of many small, distinct parts rather than one uniform substance
senses.definitionCN: 由许多细小而彼此不同的部分构成，而非单一均匀的物质
senses.example: The old farmland survives as a mosaic landscape.
senses.exampleCN: 旧农田以拼块状景观的形式留存下来。
senses.why: As an adjective the word simply states the structure that the noun implies: not one mass, but many pieces set together.
senses.whyCN: 作形容词时，这个词只是把名词所隐含的结构说出来：不是一整块，而是许多小块拼在一起。

senses.title: Unity that keeps parts visible
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：保持各部分的统一
senses.definition: any unity in which the separate contributors remain visible instead of being fused
senses.definitionCN: 任何各部分仍清晰可见、未被熔为一体的统一体
senses.example: History is a mosaic of remembered fragments, not a single stream.
senses.exampleCN: 历史是记忆碎片的拼合，而不是一条单一的河流。
senses.why: The abstract sense states what every earlier sense shares: the whole is real, but it never erases the edges of its pieces.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义说出了前面各义项的共同点：整体确实存在，但它从不抹去各小块的边界。

intro.en: Mosaic reached English through French and Italian from a Latin word for mosaic work. The Latin term is generally believed to go back to the Muse, but the chain is not fully settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: mosaic 经法语与意大利语来自一个表示「镶嵌作品」的拉丁词。这个拉丁词一般认为可追溯到「缪斯」，但整条链条并未完全定论。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin musa 'muse' came from Greek mousa. Work worthy of the Muses was called mousikos or mouseios, a word for art and learning rather than for stonework.
items.cn: 拉丁 musa「缪斯」来自希腊 mousa。配得上缪斯的作品被称作 mousikos 或 mouseios，这个词当时指艺术与学问，而不是石头工艺。

items.en: The phrase opus musivum, 'work of the Muses', is generally believed to name mosaic decoration. The adjective musaicus appears in late Latin texts beside it.
items.cn: 短语 opus musivum 意为「缪斯之作」，一般认为指镶嵌装饰。晚期拉丁文献中还有形容词 musaicus 与它并用。

items.en: Italian mosaico named both the work and the craft, and it is the form that spread through Mediterranean trade and church building.
items.cn: 意大利语 mosaico 既指作品，也指工艺；正是这个形式随地中海贸易与教堂建造传播开来。

items.en: French mosaïque carried the word into English in the sixteenth century, first for wall and floor decoration.
items.cn: 法语 mosaïque 在十六世纪把这个词带进英语，最初指墙面与地面的装饰。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word was applied to mixed societies, and later to genetics, digital images and patchy landscapes, all by the same image of separate pieces in one frame.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个词被用于混合社会，后来又用于遗传学、数字图像与斑块状景观，靠的都是「分离小块同处一框」的同一个意象。

items.en: Source uncertain: some references link the Latin adjective to Greek mouseion 'place of the Muses', while others doubt any direct derivation from the Muse at all, and no pre-Greek origin can be demonstrated.
items.cn: 来源不确定：一些资料把这个拉丁形容词与希腊 mouseion「缪斯之所」联系起来，另一些则根本怀疑它与缪斯有直接派生关系，而其希腊语之前的来源无法证明。

note.en: Group one holds near spellings with different histories; group two holds words for composite works made of many parts.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写相近但来历不同的词；第二组是同样表示「由许多部分构成的作品」的词。

entries.definition: relating to music. Music and mosaic are generally believed to share the Muse root, but the words split long before English.
entries.definitionCN: 与音乐有关的。一般认为 music 与 mosaic 共享缪斯词根，但两个词在进入英语之前早已分开。

entries.definition: a building for displaying objects of art or science. It comes from Greek mouseion, a place of the Muses, so it is a cousin rather than a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 陈列艺术或科学物品的场所。它来自希腊 mouseion「缪斯之所」，因此是远亲而非同义词。

entries.definition: a picture made by pasting paper, cloth or photographs onto a surface; the pieces stay flat and visible, unlike set stones.
entries.definitionCN: 把纸、布或照片粘贴在表面上形成的画面；各片平贴可见，不像嵌入的石子。

entries.definition: cloth made by sewing many pieces together, or any whole of mixed parts; it stresses stitching rather than setting.
entries.definitionCN: 把许多布片缝在一起做成的织物，或任何混合部分构成的整体；强调缝接而非嵌置。

entries.definition: a composite image or sequence made by cutting and joining separate shots; the joins are meant to be felt.
entries.definitionCN: 通过剪辑拼接独立镜头而成的合成画面或片段；接缝是故意让人感觉到的。

entries.definition: material set into a hollowed surface to form a design, as in wood or metal; it is close in technique but narrower in material.
entries.definitionCN: 把材料嵌进挖空的表面形成图案，如木器或金属器；技法相近，但材料范围更窄。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Latin phrase for the art meant 'work of the Muses', which links the craft to the arts rather than to building.
normal.cn: 指这门艺术的拉丁短语意为「缪斯之作」，把工艺与艺术而非建筑连在一起。

normal.en: A mosaicist is the person; mosaic is the work and the craft.
normal.cn: mosaicist 是做这件事的人；mosaic 既是作品，也是工艺。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the places where it appears: mosaic floor, mosaic pattern, glass mosaic.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出它出现的地方：镶嵌地面、镶嵌图案、玻璃马赛克。

normal.en: The social sense keeps the picture: a mosaic of cultures, a mosaic of languages.
normal.cn: 社会义保留了这个画面：文化的拼合、语言的拼合。

normal.en: Genetics uses the same word for one body made of cells from more than one line.
normal.cn: 遗传学用同一个词指一个体内含有一条以上细胞来源的身体。

abstract.en: Picture a broken plate that becomes a better picture than the whole plate ever was.
abstract.cn: 想象一只打碎的盘子，拼出的画比完整的盘子本身更好看。

abstract.en: Picture a city map where every block keeps its own colour and still reads as one city.
abstract.cn: 想象一张城市地图，每个街区保留自己的颜色，却仍读作一座城。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd photo where each face is clear at close range and only a dot from far away.
abstract.cn: 想象一张人群合影，近看每张脸都清楚，远看只是一个点。

examples.en: The restored mosaic covers the whole apse with blue and gold glass.
examples.cn: 修复后的镶嵌画用蓝金两色玻璃铺满整个半圆殿。

examples.en: The neighborhood is a mosaic of old workshops and new studios.
examples.cn: 这个街区是旧作坊与新工作室拼合成的整体。

examples.en: The software builds a mosaic from a folder of holiday photos.
examples.cn: 这款软件用一个文件夹里的假日照片拼成一幅马赛克图。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马赛克」是中文音译：一块块小砖像赛场上的队伍，拼起来才成一整幅画 → 镶嵌画

root: 经法语与意大利语上溯至晚期拉丁 opus musivum「缪斯之作」，一般认为与拉丁 musa、希腊 mousa「缪斯」有关；但直接派生链条不确定，另有与 mouseion 相联的假说，均不选定论。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one structure: many separate pieces are set into one frame. The frame can be a floor, an art form, a society, a body, a digital image, a landscape, or finally any unity that refuses to melt its parts.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项围绕同一种结构：许多分离的小块被嵌进同一个框。这个框可以是地面、一门艺术、一个社会、一个身体、一幅数字图像、一片景观，最后是任何拒绝熔掉各部分的统一体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hundreds of small stones set in mortar, each distinct, all forming one bird.
core.cn: 核心意象：数百颗小石子嵌在灰泥里，每颗都独立，合起来却是一只鸟。

branches.en: THE PICTURE: the first sense is the finished image that the pieces make.
branches.cn: 画面：第一个义项是这些小块最终拼成的成品图。

branches.en: THE CRAFT AND ITS HOME: the technique and the wall or floor it covers are the act and its place.
branches.cn: 工艺与所在：技法与它所覆盖的墙面或地面，是动作与场所。

branches.en: SOCIETY AND ABSTRACTION: a mixed society and a kept-parts unity apply the same frame to people and ideas.
branches.cn: 社会与抽象：混合社会与保留部分的统一体，把同一个框用到人与观念上。

branches.en: BODY AND IMAGE: genetics and digital pictures both assemble one whole from unlike small units.
branches.cn: 身体与图像：遗传学与数字图片都用不同的小单元拼成一个整体。

branches.en: LANDSCAPE STRUCTURE: habitat patches and the adjective describe a surface made of many distinct parts.
branches.cn: 景观结构：生境斑块与形容词义都描述由许多不同部分构成的表面。

intro.en: Mosaic is a Latin-derived word whose family is built on the Muse: the art of the Muses gave its name to the craft, and the same root reaches music and the museum.
intro.cn: mosaic 是一个源自拉丁语的词，其词族以「缪斯」为核心：缪斯的艺术给了这门工艺名称，同一词根还通到音乐与博物馆。

latinIntro.en: Latin musa and the late Latin adjective musaicus stand behind mosaic; Greek mousa is the older source, and mouseion gives museum.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 musa 与晚期拉丁形容词 musaicus 是 mosaic 的来源；更早的源头是希腊 mousa，而 mouseion 则给出 museum。

items.example: The root ties stonework to the arts of the Muses.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根把石头工艺与缪斯的艺术系在一起。

items.meaning: a Muse, a goddess of the arts
items.example: Latin musa came from Greek mousa.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁 musa 来自希腊 mousa。

items.structure: Italian mosaico, from late Latin musaicus
items.meaning: a picture set in small pieces
items.example: The floor mosaic shows a hunting scene.
items.exampleCN: 地面镶嵌画表现的是一场狩猎。

items.example: The mosaicist cut each stone by hand.
items.exampleCN: 镶嵌师亲手切割每一颗石子。

items.example: The chapel is fully mosaicked.
items.exampleCN: 这座小礼拜堂通体用镶嵌装饰。

items.meaning: the act or process of setting a mosaic
items.example: Mosaicking the vault took two years.
items.exampleCN: 给拱顶铺镶花了两年。

items.example: The field shows a mosaic-like pattern.
items.exampleCN: 田野呈现出类似镶嵌的图案。

items.example: Music and mosaic share the Muse root.
items.exampleCN: music 与 mosaic 共享缪斯词根。

items.example: The evening had a musical programme.
items.exampleCN: 晚会安排了音乐节目。

items.meaning: a building for showing art or science
items.example: The museum holds the city's mosaics.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆收藏着这座城市的镶嵌画。

latinEntries.structure: musaicus, musaica, musaicum (adj., first and second declension)
latinEntries.meaning: of mosaic work; of the Muses

definition_zh: 蚊子；蚊虫滋扰；蚊媒疾病的传播者；蚊的幼虫（作定语）；蚊帐等防蚊用品（作定语）；小型舰艇编队（蚊队）；蚊叮的小伤；被当作猎物的小飞虫（如蚊鹰）
definition_en: a small two-winged fly whose female bites and sucks blood, often carrying disease; also used of the nuisance, the diseases it spreads and small craft fleets
core_image: 水面上倒立着一只细腿小虫，口器像一根细针，背后是静止的池水与一圈涟漪
scene: 池塘边，一只蚊子把细长的口器刺进人的前臂。A mosquito pierces the skin of a sleeper's forearm with its needle-like mouthparts.
sceneCN: 这里 mosquito 指「吸血的小型双翅目昆虫」（第 1 个义项：蚊）；句意为一只蚊子用针状口器刺入睡者前臂的皮肤。可辨识物件：细长口器、透明翅膀、前臂、池水；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: A small blood-sucking fly
senses.titleCN: 蚊子：吸血的小型双翅目昆虫
senses.definition: a small two-winged fly whose female pierces skin and takes blood
senses.definitionCN: 雌虫刺穿皮肤吸血的细小双翅目昆虫
senses.example: A mosquito pierces the skin of a sleeper's forearm with its needle-like mouthparts.
senses.exampleCN: 一只蚊子用针状口器刺入睡者前臂的皮肤。
senses.why: Only the female bites, because she needs blood protein for her eggs; the everyday word still names the whole insect.
senses.whyCN: 只有雌虫叮咬，因为它需要血液中的蛋白质来产卵；日常用词仍指整个虫体。

senses.title: A biting nuisance
senses.definition: mosquitoes treated collectively as an irritating swarm that drives people indoors
senses.definitionCN: 把蚊虫看成一群扰人的飞虫，能把人赶进屋里
senses.example: The mosquitoes drove the whole camp indoors before dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 蚊群还没到黄昏就把整个营地的人赶进了屋。
senses.why: When the plural is used this way, the word names an annoyance rather than a species.
senses.whyCN: 复数这样用时，词指的是扰人的麻烦，而不是某个物种。

senses.title: A disease vector
senses.definition: the insect understood as the carrier that passes malaria, dengue or other infections between people
senses.definitionCN: 被理解为在人与人之间传递疟疾、登革热等感染的媒介昆虫
senses.example: Mosquitoes carry malaria in lowland regions.
senses.exampleCN: 蚊子在低地地区传播疟疾。
senses.why: Public health shifted the emphasis from the bite to the transmission chain, and this sense now dominates medical writing.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生把重点从叮咬转到传播链，这一义如今在医学写作中占主导。

senses.title: The aquatic young stage
senses.definition: the larval form that hangs at the water surface, usually named in the compound mosquito larva
senses.definitionCN: 倒悬在水面的幼虫，通常以「mosquito larva」这一复合形式出现
senses.example: Mosquito larvae hang head-down just beneath the surface film.
senses.exampleCN: 孑孓头朝下挂在表面水膜之下。
senses.why: The adult name is reused as a modifier for its own young, a common pattern in entomology.
senses.whyCN: 成虫名被复用作自身幼期的修饰语，这是昆虫学中常见的模式。

senses.title: Protective gear against mosquitoes
senses.definition: the equipment named after the insect, such as a mosquito net, coil or repellent
senses.definitionCN: 以这种昆虫命名的防护用品，如蚊帐、蚊香或驱蚊剂
senses.example: A mosquito net over the bed is the cheapest protection.
senses.exampleCN: 床上挂一顶蚊帐是最便宜的防护。
senses.why: The word marks what the object is used against, so the insect name becomes a label for the defence.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标出物件用来对付什么，昆虫名于是成了防护手段的标签。

senses.title: A fleet of small craft
senses.definition: a group of tiny, fast boats or warships, historically called a mosquito fleet
senses.definitionCN: 一群小而快的船或军舰，历史上称作蚊队
senses.example: A mosquito fleet of wooden gunboats patrolled the river.
senses.exampleCN: 一支由木制炮艇组成的蚊队巡弋河面。
senses.why: The metaphor compares small, numerous, stinging craft to a swarm of biting insects.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把数量多、体量小、能刺痛人的舰艇比作一群叮人的虫。

senses.title: A small irritating wound
senses.definition: the itchy swelling left by a bite, commonly called a mosquito bite
senses.definitionCN: 叮咬留下的发痒肿块，通常说成「mosquito bite」
senses.example: A mosquito bite on his ankle kept him awake.
senses.exampleCN: 脚踝上的蚊叮让他一夜没睡好。
senses.why: Metonymy moves the name from the biter to the mark it leaves, a very common shift in medical everyday speech.
senses.whyCN: 转喻把名字从叮咬者移到留下的痕迹，这是医学口语中极常见的转移。

senses.title: A tiny flying prey
senses.titleCN: 被当作猎物的小飞虫（如蚊鹰）
senses.definition: a small flying insect understood as food for a predator, as in the folk name mosquito hawk
senses.definitionCN: 被看作捕食者食物的小飞虫，如俗称蚊鹰的蜻蜓
senses.example: Children call the dragonfly a mosquito hawk because it catches small flies.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们把蜻蜓叫作蚊鹰，因为它捕食小飞虫。
senses.why: Here mosquito names the prey, and the compound tells what the larger insect feeds on.
senses.whyCN: 此处 mosquito 指猎物，复合词说明那种更大的昆虫吃什么。

intro.en: Mosquito is a Spanish and Portuguese diminutive of mosca 'fly', from Latin musca. English borrowed it in the sixteenth century during exploration of the Americas.
intro.cn: mosquito 是西班牙语与葡萄牙语中 mosca「苍蝇」的指小形式，源自拉丁 musca。英语在 16 世纪探索美洲期间把它借入。

items.en: Latin musca meant 'fly'; its own deeper origin is not settled, and the Indo-European forms sometimes cited for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: 拉丁 musca 意为「苍蝇」；它更深的来源并无定论，偶尔为其引用的印欧形式属重构。

items.en: Spanish and Portuguese added the diminutive suffix -ito to mosca, giving mosquito 'little fly', the form English borrowed.
items.cn: 西班牙语与葡萄牙语给 mosca 加上指小后缀 -ito，构成 mosquito「小苍蝇」，英语借的就是这一形式。

items.en: English recorded mosquito in the late sixteenth century in travel accounts of the Caribbean and South America.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪后期的加勒比与南美游记中记录了 mosquito。

items.en: After the discovery that the insect transmits malaria and yellow fever, the word moved into public health vocabulary in the late nineteenth century.
items.cn: 在发现这种昆虫传播疟疾与黄热病之后，这个词于 19 世纪后期进入公共卫生词汇。

items.en: Both mosquitoes and mosquitos are accepted plurals; the longer form follows the older English habit of doubling the final consonant before -es.
items.cn: mosquitoes 与 mosquitos 两种复数都被接受；较长的一种沿用英语在 -es 前双写末尾辅音的老习惯。

items.en: Source uncertain (detail and first date): the deeper origin and the exact first citation are not settled, so any pre-Latin form offered here is a reconstruction and competing hypotheses are left side by side.
items.cn: 来源不确定（细节与首见年代）：更深的来源与确切最早书证均无定论，此处给出的拉丁语之前形式属重构形式，并列假说一并保留、不作定论。

note.en: Group one collects words that look or sound close but come from other roots; group two collects the small biting flies people mix up with mosquitoes.
note.cn: 第一组收形近音近但来源不同的词；第二组收人们常与蚊子混淆的小型叮咬蝇类。

entries.definition: Mosque comes from Arabic masjid, a place of prostration; the resemblance to mosquito is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: mosque 来自阿拉伯语 masjid，意为叩拜之处；与 mosquito 的相似纯属偶然。

entries.definition: Miskito names a people and a coast of Central America and is spelled with a k; it is not the insect.
entries.definitionCN: Miskito 指中美洲的一个民族与一片海岸，拼写带 k，不是这种昆虫。

entries.definition: This plural is a spelling variant of mosquitoes, not a different word with a different meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 这个复数只是 mosquitoes 的拼写变体，并非意义不同的另一个词。

entries.definition: The compound names the bed net, so the insect word is working as a modifier rather than as the subject.
entries.definitionCN: 这个复合词指床上用的蚊帐，昆虫词在此作修饰语而非主语。

entries.definition: A gnat is a very small biting fly, often a midge; it bites but does not transmit malaria.
entries.definitionCN: gnat 指极小的叮咬蝇，常为蠓；会叮人但不传播疟疾。

entries.definition: A midge is a minute two-winged fly, some species of which bite in swarms near water.
entries.definitionCN: midge 是极小的双翅目蝇，有些种类在水边成群叮人。

entries.definition: Fly is the general name for the order, of which the mosquito is one family.
entries.definitionCN: fly 是这一目的通称，蚊子只是其中一科。

entries.definition: A flea is a wingless jumping insect that bites; it belongs to a different order entirely.
entries.definitionCN: flea 是无翅跳跃的叮咬昆虫，属于完全不同的目。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Spanish mosca 'fly' plus the diminutive -ito gives mosquito, literally 'little fly'.
normal.cn: 西班牙语 mosca「苍蝇」加指小后缀 -ito 构成 mosquito，字面就是「小苍蝇」。

normal.en: The family runs mosquito, mosquitoes, mosquitos, mosquitofish and mosquitocide.
normal.cn: 词族包括 mosquito、mosquitoes、mosquitos、mosquitofish 与 mosquitocide。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: mosquito net, mosquito coil, mosquito-borne disease.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：蚊帐、蚊香、蚊媒疾病。

normal.en: Only the female bites; males feed on nectar.
normal.cn: 只有雌虫叮咬，雄虫吸食花蜜。

normal.en: The larval stage is the wriggler that hangs at the water surface.
normal.cn: 幼虫期就是倒悬在水面的孑孓。

abstract.en: Picture a needle so fine that the sleeper never feels it enter.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细到睡者完全察觉不到的针。

abstract.en: Picture a whole village sleeping under white gauze, one net per bed.
abstract.cn: 想象整个村子睡在白纱之下，每张床一顶帐。

abstract.en: Picture a hundred small boats stinging a harbour like a swarm.
abstract.cn: 想象上百条小船像虫群一样刺痛一座港口。

examples.en: The mosquito net was treated with insecticide and hung over both beds.
examples.cn: 蚊帐经杀虫剂处理，挂在两张床的上方。

examples.en: Mosquitoes breeding in standing water made the drainage project urgent.
examples.cn: 蚊子在积水中繁殖，使排水工程变得紧迫。

examples.en: A mosquito bite on her wrist swelled into a hard red lump.
examples.cn: 她手腕上的蚊叮肿成了一个硬红的包。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mosquito（莫斯基托）」——在池边「莫」名其妙被叮一口的小虫 → 蚊子

root: 西班牙语/葡萄牙语 mosquito「小苍蝇」= mosca「苍蝇」+ 指小后缀 -ito；mosca 源自拉丁 musca「苍蝇」。拉丁 musca 更早来源不确定，所引印欧形式属重构形式。与 mosque（阿拉伯语 masjid）无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from the biting insect, spread to the swarm, the disease chain, its water-borne young, the gear used against it, small warships, the mark it leaves and the prey it becomes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从叮人的昆虫出发，扩展到虫群、疾病链、水中幼期、对付它的器物、小型舰艇、留下的包以及它作为猎物的一面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle-thin mouthpart breaking the skin while a gauze net hangs above the bed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细如针的口器刺破皮肤，床的上方挂着纱帐。

branches.en: THE BITE: the insect and the itchy mark it leaves are two ends of one act.
branches.cn: 叮咬：昆虫与它留下的痒包是同一动作的两端。

branches.en: THE SWARM: the nuisance and the wriggling young both present the insect in numbers.
branches.cn: 虫群：扰人的成蚊与扭动的幼虫都以数量呈现这种昆虫。

branches.en: TRANSMISSION: the bite becomes a link in a chain between patients.
branches.cn: 传播：叮咬成为病人之间链条上的一环。

branches.en: DEFENCE AND METAPHOR: nets and coils answer the bite, and small fast boats borrow it.
branches.cn: 防护与比喻：蚊帐蚊香回应叮咬，小而快的船借用了它。

branches.en: THE PREY: the name finally marks a food item for a larger hunter.
branches.cn: 猎物：名字最后标出一种更大捕食者的食物。

intro.en: Mosquito is a Spanish diminutive built on a Latin root; its English derivatives are compounds, while the Latin family supplies the technical terms.
intro.cn: mosquito 是在拉丁词根上构成的西班牙语指小词；英语派生词多为复合，技术术语则来自拉丁词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin musca 'fly' gives muscid and musciform in zoology; the Spanish diminutive is the branch that produced the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 musca「苍蝇」在动物学中给出 muscid 与 musciform；产生英语名词的是西班牙语指小这一支。

items.example: A mosquito rests on the shaded wall.
items.exampleCN: 一只蚊子在背阴的墙上停歇。

items.example: Mosquitoes breed wherever water stands.
items.exampleCN: 凡有积水处蚊子就能繁殖。

items.meaning: a net hung over a bed
items.example: The mosquito net kept the room quiet at night.
items.exampleCN: 蚊帐让夜里屋里安静下来。

items.example: A mosquito coil smoked in the corner.
items.exampleCN: 角落里点着一盘蚊香。

items.meaning: a substance that keeps the insect off
items.example: The mosquito repellent smelled of lemon grass.
items.exampleCN: 驱蚊剂有柠檬草的味道。

items.meaning: a small fish that eats larvae
items.example: Mosquitofish were introduced to clear the ponds.
items.exampleCN: 人们引入食蚊鱼来清理池塘。

items.meaning: a substance that kills the insect
items.example: The spray is a mosquitocide for drains.
items.exampleCN: 这种喷雾是用于排水沟的灭蚊剂。

items.example: A mosquito hawk hovered over the path.
items.exampleCN: 一只蚊鹰在小径上方悬停。

items.example: Malaria is a mosquito-borne infection.
items.exampleCN: 疟疾是一种蚊媒感染。

definition_zh: 主要地；大部分；通常；几乎全部
definition_en: for the greatest part of a group or amount; in most cases or most of the time; and almost entirely
core_image: 一只盘子里大半装着米饭，边角只留几样小菜
scene: 傍晚的自助餐厅里，长桌大半已经空了，只有靠窗那几盘菜还被夹得七零八落。By eight the buffet was quiet, and the trays that were mostly empty had been stacked by the door.
sceneCN: 这里是「大半、大部分」（第 1 个义项：指一个整体中的多数部分）；句意为到八点时自助餐区已经安静下来，那些大半空了的托盘被叠在门边。图中可辨识物件：长餐台、成摞的托盘、靠窗的菜盘。

pos.zh: 主要地；大部分；通常；几乎全部

derivatives.zh: 与 mostly 同源的基础词，去掉副词后缀 -ly 即得，义为「最多的；大多数的」
由古英语 eall（全部）与 māst（最多）缩合而成，义为「几乎」，与 most 同源
由古英语 ūt（向外）加 most 构成，义为「最远的；极度的」

senses.title: The greatest share of a group
senses.definition: applying to the greater number of people or things in a group
senses.definitionCN: 适用于一个群体中数量占多数的人或物
senses.example: The guests at the wedding were mostly relatives from her side.
senses.exampleCN: 婚礼上的宾客多半是她这边的亲戚。
senses.why: The word is built on the Old English superlative māst, the greatest share, so its first duty is to report how a whole divides rather than to name a frequency.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在古英语最高级 māst（最大的份额）上，所以它首先管的是「一个整体怎么分」，而不是说事情多久发生一次。

senses.title: In most cases, as a habit
senses.definition: happening on most occasions, though not on every one
senses.definitionCN: 在多数场合都会发生，但并非每一次
senses.example: He mostly takes the early train and reads on the way.
senses.exampleCN: 他通常坐早班车，在路上看书。
senses.why: Once the word could mark the larger part of anything, it could also mark the larger part of a routine, which is how a share of a group turned into a habitual frequency.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词能标出任何事物里较大的那部分，它也就能标出日常习惯里较大的那部分，群体份额就这样长成了习惯性的频率。

senses.title: Nearly the whole of an amount
senses.definition: covering the largest part of a quantity or substance, with only a small remainder
senses.definitionCN: 占去数量或物质的最大部分，只剩下很少一点
senses.example: The bottle in the shed is mostly rainwater.
senses.exampleCN: 棚子里那瓶装的几乎全是雨水。
senses.why: Measuring a substance leaves a visible remainder, so the same superlative sense reads as a near total: the greatest share of a bottle is almost the bottle, and the rest is an exception.
senses.whyCN: 给一样东西计量时总会剩下一小点，于是同一个最高级的意思读成了「接近全部」：一只瓶子里的最大份额就是几乎整瓶，剩下那点只是例外。

intro.en: Mostly is an Old English superlative turned into an adverb: most, the greatest share, plus the ending -ly, which says in what manner a statement holds.
intro.cn: mostly 是古英语最高级加副词词尾构成的词：most 指最大的份额，-ly 表示一句话以什么方式成立。

items.en: Māst was the superlative of micel, great, and it named the greatest amount or the greatest share of a group.
items.cn: māst 是 micel（大的）的最高级，指最大的数量，或一个群体中最大的份额。

items.en: The ending -līce came from līc, body or form, and it turned an adjective into an adverb meaning in the manner of something; in English it settled as -ly.
items.cn: -līce 这个词尾出自 līc（身体、形貌），把形容词变成表示「以……方式」的副词；进入英语后固定为 -ly。

items.en: Middle English joined most and -ly into mostli, an adverb reporting what holds for the greater number of cases.
items.cn: 中古英语把 most 与 -ly 合成 mostli，用作副词，表示对多数情形都成立。

items.en: By the fifteenth century mostly was common in the sense of for the greatest part, and it stood beside almost, which had grown from all and most.
items.cn: 到十五世纪，mostly 已常见，意为「大部分」；它与由 all 与 most 合成的 almost 并列使用。

items.en: Modern English keeps three readings: a share of a group, a habitual frequency, and a near total in amount, and dictionaries list them as separate senses.
items.cn: 现代英语保留三种读法：群体中的份额、习惯性的频率、数量上接近全部；词典把它们分列为不同义项。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the Old English words that share the most element; the near-meaning group collects adverbs of majority and frequency.
note.cn: 形近组收与 most 共用词素的古英语词与英语词；近义组收表示多数与频率的副词。

entries.definition: The greatest amount, or the greater number of a group.
entries.definitionCN: 最大的数量，或一个群体中的多数。

entries.definition: Not quite, but very nearly.
entries.definitionCN: 差一点，但非常接近。

entries.definition: Farthest out, or greatest in degree.
entries.definitionCN: 最远的，或程度最大的。

entries.definition: Ranking first in importance or position.
entries.definitionCN: 在重要性或位置上居首的。

entries.definition: More than anything else, or for the greater part.
entries.definitionCN: 首要地，或大部分情况下。

entries.definition: To a great extent.
entries.definitionCN: 在很大程度上。

entries.definition: In most cases or on most occasions.
entries.definitionCN: 多数情况下，或多数场合。

entries.definition: Above all; mostly but not only.
entries.definitionCN: 首先；主要是，但不只是。

normalIntro.en: The word is one Old English superlative plus one adverbial ending, and everything about it follows from the idea of the greatest share.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是一个古英语最高级加一个副词词尾，它的全部用法都从「最大份额」这个想法里长出来。

normal.en: Most is the superlative of great, so mostly begins with the idea of the greatest share, not with a vague idea of many.
normal.cn: most 是 great 的最高级，所以 mostly 的起点是「最大份额」，而不是笼统的「很多」。

normal.en: -ly comes from an Old English word for body or form, and it turns an adjective into a statement about manner.
normal.cn: -ly 出自古英语里表示身体或形貌的词，它把形容词变成说明「方式」的词。

normal.en: Almost is all plus most, a near total, and it sits beside mostly in the same family of degree words.
normal.cn: almost 是 all 加 most，表示接近全部，它与 mostly 并排站在同一族程度词里。

normal.en: Weather reports say mostly sunny because the forecast covers most of a region and most of a day, not every square metre or every minute.
normal.cn: 天气预报说 mostly sunny，因为预报覆盖的是一个地区的大部分和一天的大部分，而不是每一平方米、每一分钟。

normal.en: Mostly because names the leading reason among several, which is the same share logic applied to causes instead of things.
normal.cn: mostly because 指几个原因里最主要的那个，这正是把「份额」的逻辑从事物挪到了原因。

abstract.en: Picture a plate where rice fills most of the surface and two small side dishes take the corners.
abstract.cn: 想象一只盘子，米饭占去大半个盘面，两样小菜只占边角。

abstract.en: A word for the largest share keeps the minority visible: mostly means not entirely, so the rest is still there.
abstract.cn: 一个表示最大份额的词始终让少数派可见：mostly 意为「并非全部」，剩下的部分仍在。

abstract.en: Because it measures shares rather than absolutes, mostly fits sentences that report, estimate and predict, from weather to polls.
abstract.cn: 因为它衡量的是份额而不是绝对，mostly 特别适合报告、估计和预测的句子，从天气到民调都是。

examples.en: The trays on the counter were mostly empty by eight.
examples.cn: 到八点时，柜台上的托盘大半已经空了。

examples.en: She mostly works from home on Fridays.
examples.cn: 她周五通常在家工作。

examples.en: The report is mostly accurate, with two figures out of date.
examples.cn: 这份报告大体准确，只有两个数字过时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莫斯特里」——大半时间都在忙，只剩一点才歇；记住 mostly 是大半、通常、几乎全部。

root: 古英语 māst（最多的，micel 的最高级）加副词词尾 -līce（后作 -ly）构成 mostli，中古英语起意为「大部分」；同族词有 most、almost、utmost、foremost，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the largest share; the senses divide into a share of a group, a habitual frequency, and a near total in amount.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是最大份额；义项分出群体中的多数、习惯性的频率，以及数量上的接近全部。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plate where one dish covers most of the surface and small portions sit at the edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只盘子，一样菜占去大半，边上只留几小份。

branches.en: a tray with a few crumbs left on it
branches.cn: 只剩几点碎屑的托盘

branches.en: a hall where most seats are taken
branches.cn: 大半座位已坐了人的礼堂

branches.en: the early train taken on every working morning
branches.cn: 每个工作日早晨都坐的那班早车

branches.en: a bottle holding water with a thin layer of oil on top
branches.cn: 瓶里几乎全是水，只浮着一薄层油

branches.en: one adverb covering both how often a thing happens and how much of it there is
branches.cn: 同一个副词，既管事情多久发生一次，也管一样东西占了多少

intro.en: One Old English superlative, one adverbial ending and the English words built from them hold the entry together.
intro.cn: 一个古英语最高级、一个副词词尾，以及由它们构成的英语词，把这个词条撑了起来。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded: mostly belongs to the Old English stock of degree words, and its relatives are Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录：mostly 属于古英语的程度词系统，其亲属词来自日耳曼语。

definition_zh: 蛾；蛾类；（衣物等的）蛀虫；蛾状物
definition_en: a mainly night-flying insect related to the butterfly, with wings that are usually held flat and antennae without clubs
core_image: 一只灰褐色的蛾贴着墙停在灯下，翅平摊成一片薄瓦，粉末状的鳞在手一抹就掉
scene: 夜里灯一亮，窗玻璃上就贴满了灰扑扑的翅膀。 A pale moth circled the lamp three times before settling on the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 moth 指「蛾」（第 1 个义项：多夜间活动、停歇时翅平展的鳞翅目昆虫）；句意为一只浅色蛾绕灯三圈，最后停在墙上。

pos.zh: 蛾的；被蛾蛀坏的（多用于复合词）

derivatives.zh: 满是蛾的；有蛾蛀痕迹的

senses.title: The night-flying relative of the butterfly
senses.titleCN: 蝴蝶的近亲，多在夜间活动
senses.definition: an insect of the order Lepidoptera that is usually active at night and rests with wings spread flat
senses.definitionCN: 鳞翅目中通常夜间活动、停歇时平展双翅的昆虫
senses.example: A pale moth circled the lamp three times.
senses.exampleCN: 一只浅色蛾绕灯转了三圈。
senses.why: the word has meant this animal since Old English, and everything else it names is taken from the insect's habits or its damage.
senses.whyCN: 这个词自上古英语起就指这种动物，其它所指都取自它的习性或其造成的损害。

senses.title: The whole group contrasted with butterflies
senses.titleCN: 与蝴蝶相对的整个类群
senses.definition: the nocturnal division of the Lepidoptera, as a category in classification and in counts
senses.definitionCN: 鳞翅目中的夜间类群，作为分类与计数中的一个类别
senses.example: Moths outnumber butterflies in almost every habitat.
senses.exampleCN: 在几乎所有生境中，蛾的数量都超过蝴蝶。
senses.why: as a category the word is plural and uncountable in practice, because the point is the group, not one animal.
senses.whyCN: 作为类别，这个词实际上用复数且近乎不可数，因为重点是群体而非一只。

senses.title: The household clothes moth
senses.definition: a small species whose larvae eat wool, fur and stored fabric
senses.definitionCN: 幼虫取食羊毛、毛皮与储存织物的小型物种
senses.example: A moth had eaten a hole through the sleeve.
senses.exampleCN: 一只衣蛾在袖子上蛀出一个洞。
senses.why: the everyday sense narrows to the one species that enters houses and causes loss.
senses.whyCN: 日常义收窄到那一种进入住宅并造成损失的物种。

senses.title: Damage described as moth-eaten
senses.definition: the state of fabric or fur that has been holed by moth larvae
senses.definitionCN: 织物或毛皮被蛾类幼虫蛀出孔洞的状态
senses.example: The coat was moth-eaten at the collar.
senses.exampleCN: 这件外套的领子被虫蛀了。
senses.why: the insect's name becomes an adjective for its effect, so damage is described by its cause.
senses.whyCN: 昆虫名转为描述其效果的形容词，因此损坏由起因来描述。

senses.title: A ball that keeps moths away
senses.definition: a small ball of a strong-smelling chemical placed among stored clothes to repel moths
senses.definitionCN: 放在储存衣物之间、以强烈气味驱蛾的小球
senses.example: She put a moth ball in each wool blanket.
senses.exampleCN: 她在每条羊毛毯里放了一颗防蛾丸。
senses.why: the compound names the object by the insect it repels, a common pattern in household vocabulary.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词以它所驱赶的昆虫来命名物件，这是家用词汇中常见的模式。

senses.title: To mothball a ship or a plan
senses.definition: to put a ship, factory or plan into storage, out of use but kept in condition
senses.definitionCN: 把船、工厂或计划封存起来，停用但保持状态
senses.example: The fleet was mothballed for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这支船队被封存了十年。
senses.why: the verb grew from the noun mothball, and then generalized to any suspended project.
senses.whyCN: 动词由名词 mothball 长出，随后泛化到任何被搁置的项目。

senses.title: Attraction to a light trap
senses.definition: the habit of moths flying to artificial light, used in survey traps
senses.definitionCN: 蛾飞向人造光源的习性，被用于调查诱捕
senses.example: The moth trap ran all night and filled with hundreds of species.
senses.exampleCN: 诱蛾灯整夜开着，装满了数百个物种。
senses.why: the word stands for the animal whose behaviour defines the method.
senses.whyCN: 这个词代表那类动物，而其习性定义了这种方法。

senses.title: Figurative: drawn toward one's own harm
senses.titleCN: 比喻：被引向自身的毁灭
senses.definition: figurative, a person or thing irresistibly attracted to what will destroy it
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指被必将毁灭自己之物不可抗拒地吸引的人或事物
senses.example: He went to the meeting like a moth to a flame.
senses.exampleCN: 他去赴会，像飞蛾扑火一样。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps two features only: attraction and self-destruction, dropping the insect.
senses.whyCN: 比喻只保留两个特征：被吸引与自我毁灭，昆虫本身被舍去。

intro.en: Moth is an Old English word with Germanic relatives and a disputed deeper origin; the related sense of clothes damage is medieval.
intro.cn: moth 是古英语词，有日耳曼同族词，更深来源有争议；与衣物损害相关的义项为中世纪所出。

items.en: Old English moththe meant both the insect and the larva that eats cloth, a double sense the modern word keeps.
items.cn: 古英语 moththe 既指昆虫，也指吃布的幼虫，现代词保留了这双重含义。

items.en: Old Norse motti, Middle Dutch mot and German Motte point to a common Germanic stock rather than a borrowing.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 motti、中古荷兰语 mot、德语 Motte 表明共同的日耳曼来源，而非借词。

items.en: Source uncertain (root): the pre-Germanic origin of moth is unresolved; a link to a word for a maggot or for a gnawing creature has been suggested but not demonstrated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根）：moth 在日耳曼语之前的来源无定论；与「蛆」或「啃咬者」某词的联系属提议，未获得证明。

items.en: From the medieval period the word was applied to the small cloth-eating species, and mothball followed in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 自中世纪起这个词用于吃布的小型物种，mothball 于 19 世纪随之出现。

items.en: Mothball became a verb meaning to store and preserve, later extended to any suspended plan.
items.cn: mothball 转为动词，意为封存保存，后扩展至任何被搁置的计划。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest record of the figurative 'moth to a flame' use is not firmly dated, so the dating here is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：比喻义「飞蛾扑火」的最早记录年代不详，此处年代为约数。

note.en: Group one separates moth from the insects it is confused with; group two separates it from the words built on its name.
note.cn: 第一组区分 moth 与易混昆虫；第二组区分它与建在其名上的词。

entries.definition: Flies by day, antennae club-tipped, wings held together at rest; the everyday dividing line between the two groups.
entries.definitionCN: 白天飞行、触角棒状、停歇时合翅；这是两群之间的日常分界。

entries.definition: Describes fabric holed by larvae, and figuratively anything worn out or stale.
entries.definitionCN: 描述被幼虫蛀出孔的织物，比喻义指陈旧破败之物。

entries.definition: As a noun a repellent ball, as a verb to store something out of use.
entries.definitionCN: 名词指驱蛾球，动词指把某物封存停用。

entries.definition: The caterpillar of a domesticated moth; the adult is a moth, but the economic word is for the larva.
entries.definitionCN: 家养蛾的幼虫；成虫是蛾，但经济用词指的是幼虫。

entries.definition: Larva is the feeding stage of any insect; the cloth-damaging moth is only the larval stage of a small species.
entries.definitionCN: larva 是任何昆虫的取食阶段；蛀布者只是某一小型种的幼虫阶段。

entries.definition: A midge is a small two-winged fly, not a moth; the confusion comes from size and night flight.
entries.definitionCN: midge 是小型双翅蝇类，不是蛾；混淆来自体型与夜间飞行。

entries.definition: A general word for a small crawling insect; it carries none of the night-flight or cloth-eating detail.
entries.definitionCN: 小爬虫的泛称，不含夜飞或蛀布的细节。

entries.definition: Vermin is a category of harmful animals; a moth is vermin only when it damages stored goods.
entries.definitionCN: vermin 是有害动物的类别；蛾只在损害储存物时才算。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Germanic relatives, real compounds and real idioms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实日耳曼同族词、真实复合词与真实习语。

normal.en: The Germanic relatives are Old Norse motti, Middle Dutch mot and German Motte.
normal.cn: 日耳曼同族词是古诺斯语 motti、中古荷兰语 mot、德语 Motte。

normal.en: The family runs moth, moths, mothball, moth-eaten, mothproof, moth trap.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 moth、moths、mothball、moth-eaten、mothproof、moth trap。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: clothes moth, silkworm moth, moth species.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：衣蛾、蚕蛾、蛾类物种。

normal.en: The idiom like a moth to a flame is the standard figurative use.
normal.cn: 习语 「like a moth to a flame」是标准比喻用法。

normal.en: Moths hold their wings flat; butterflies close theirs.
normal.cn: 蛾平展双翅；蝴蝶合起。

abstract.en: Picture a dust of scales left on a hand after one touch.
abstract.cn: 想象一触之后留在手上的那层鳞粉。

abstract.en: Picture a coat kept for thirty years with three holes in the collar.
abstract.cn: 想象一件存了三十年的外套，领子上三个洞。

abstract.en: Picture a light so bright that it ends the flyer.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏亮到足以终结飞者的灯。

examples.en: Most moths are active only after the light fails.
examples.cn: 多数蛾只在光线消失之后活动。

examples.en: The specimen drawer was sealed to keep moths out.
examples.cn: 标本抽屉密封起来，以防蛾进入。

examples.en: They mothballed the plant rather than sell it.
examples.cn: 他们选择封存工厂，而不是出售。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「moth」——夜里绕灯、翅上掉粉、还蛀衣服的虫 → 蛾

root: 古英语 moththe「蛾；吃布的幼虫」，与古诺斯语 motti、中古荷兰语 mot、德语 Motte 同出日耳曼词；日耳曼语之前词根来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one night flyer: a flat-winged insect comes to the lamp, and the word then names a whole category, a household pest, its damage, the ball that repels it, the act of storing something away, a survey method, and finally a figure for self-destructive attraction.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一只夜行飞虫展开：平翅昆虫来到灯下；词语随后指整个类群、家中害虫、它造成的损坏、驱它的丸球、把东西封存起来的行为、一种调查方法，最后指自毁式吸引的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey-brown flyer pressed flat against the wall under a lamp.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只灰褐色飞虫在灯下平贴墙上。

branches.en: ANIMAL AND CATEGORY: one insect, then the group it belongs to.
branches.cn: 动物与类别：一只昆虫，然后是它所属的群。

branches.en: HOUSEHOLD LOSS: the small species and the holes it leaves.
branches.cn: 家中损失：小型物种与它留下的洞。

branches.en: REPELLENT AND STORAGE: the ball first keeps moths away, then names putting things away.
branches.cn: 驱避与封存：丸球先把蛾赶走，随后指把东西收起来。

branches.en: METHOD: the animal's attraction becomes a survey tool.
branches.cn: 方法：动物的趋光性成为调查工具。

branches.en: SELF-DESTRUCTION: the flame image survives without the insect.
branches.cn: 自我毁灭：火的意象留存，昆虫被舍去。

intro.en: Moth is a bare Germanic noun that forms compounds rather than taking Latin affixes.
intro.cn: moth 是裸露的日耳曼名词，主要构成复合词，而不接拉丁词缀。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is present; the Latin entries below are the learned nouns for moth and for the order it belongs to.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不含拉丁成分；下列拉丁条目是蛾及其所属目的学术名称。

items.example: A moth came in through the open window.
items.exampleCN: 一只蛾从开着的窗进来。

items.example: Moths filled the trap by midnight.
items.exampleCN: 到午夜诱捕器已装满蛾。

items.example: The blanket was moth-eaten.
items.exampleCN: 毯子被虫蛀了。

items.example: Mothballs smell of camphor.
items.exampleCN: 防蛾丸有樟脑味。

items.example: The wool was mothproofed before storage.
items.exampleCN: 羊毛在储存前做了防蛀处理。

items.meaning: a device that attracts and catches moths
items.example: The moth trap ran from dusk to dawn.
items.exampleCN: 诱蛾灯从黄昏开到黎明。

items.example: Clothes moths avoid light.
items.exampleCN: 衣蛾避光。

items.meaning: the adult of the silk-producing species
items.example: The silkworm moth cannot fly well.
items.exampleCN: 蚕蛾飞行能力差。

items.meaning: full of moths, or marked by moth damage
items.example: The attic smelled mothy.
items.exampleCN: 阁楼里有股蛀虫味。

latinEntries.meaning: a clothes moth, a gnawing worm

definition_zh: 运动；移动；动作；手势；动议；提议；机械运转；排便；用手势示意
definition_en: the act or process of moving, or a movement of the hand that signals something, or a formal proposal put to a meeting
core_image: 一枚棋子被手指从棋盘一格推到下一格，棋后拖出一道浅痕
scene: 会议开到一半，有人从座位上站起，把一页提案放到桌上，请全场表决。She rose to put a motion to the committee.
sceneCN: 这里 motion 指提交会议表决的正式提议（第 3 个义项：动议）；句意：她起身向委员会提出一项动议。图中可辨识物件：提案纸页、会议桌、木槌、座位牌；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 运动；移动；手势；动议；机械运转

senses.title: Change of position
senses.definition: the process of changing position or place over time
senses.definitionCN: 随时间改变位置或处所的过程
senses.example: The motion of the pendulum is regular and easy to time.
senses.exampleCN: 钟摆的运动很规律，容易计时。
senses.why: Latin motio is simply a moving, from movere 'to move'; this is the plainest and oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 motio 就是「移动」，出自 movere「移动」；这是最直白、最古老的义项。

senses.title: A gesture that carries a message
senses.definition: a movement of the hand or head used instead of words to signal something
senses.definitionCN: 代替言语、用来示意的手部或头部动作
senses.example: With a quick motion of his hand, the conductor silenced the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 指挥手一挥，大厅便静了下来。
senses.why: A gesture is a small movement that does the work of a sentence.
senses.whyCN: 手势是一个小动作，却承担了一句话的功能。

senses.title: A proposal put to a meeting
senses.definition: a formal proposal presented at a meeting for discussion and a vote
senses.definitionCN: 在会议上正式提出、供讨论并表决的提议
senses.example: The motion to extend the deadline was carried by nine votes.
senses.exampleCN: 延长截止日期的动议以九票通过。
senses.why: To bring something forward is to move it onto the table; the proposal is the thing set in motion before the room.
senses.whyCN: 把某事提出来，就是把它移到桌面上；提议就是被推到全场面前的东西。

senses.title: A request made to a court
senses.titleCN: 向法庭提出的程序申请
senses.definition: a formal request asking a court to make a ruling or take an action
senses.definitionCN: 请求法庭作出裁定或采取行动正式申请
senses.example: The defence filed a motion to dismiss the charge.
senses.exampleCN: 辩方提交了撤销指控的动议。
senses.why: A court, like an assembly, decides only what is moved before it, so the legal request kept the parliamentary name.
senses.whyCN: 法庭和议会一样，只裁决被推到它面前的事，因此法律申请沿用了议会里的名称。

senses.title: The act of starting a process
senses.definition: the act of setting a plan, process or event going
senses.definitionCN: 使计划、进程或事件开始运转的动作
senses.example: One phone call set the whole rescue in motion.
senses.exampleCN: 一个电话启动了整场救援。
senses.why: The fixed phrase set in motion treats a process as a body that must be pushed before it will move.
senses.whyCN: 「使……启动」这一固定说法把进程当作一具必须先推一把才会动的身体。

senses.title: The running of a machine
senses.definition: the working movement of a machine or mechanism, or its state of running
senses.definitionCN: 机器或机构的运转动作，或其正在运行的状态
senses.example: The old lift was in motion again after the belt was replaced.
senses.exampleCN: 换过皮带后，老电梯又运转起来。
senses.why: A machine is a body whose parts move, so its operation is naturally called motion.
senses.whyCN: 机器是一具有部件在动的身体，因此它的运行自然被叫作 motion。

senses.title: The moving works inside a device
senses.definition: the assembly of moving parts inside a device, especially a clock or watch
senses.definitionCN: 装置内部由运动部件组成的机构，尤指钟表机芯
senses.example: A watchmaker cleaned the motion and oiled each pivot.
senses.exampleCN: 钟表匠清理了机芯，并给每个轴心上了油。
senses.why: Watchmakers named the works by the movement they produce, and the term became the trade word for the whole mechanism.
senses.whyCN: 钟表匠以它所产生的运动来命名这套机构，这个说法后来成了整个机芯的行业词。

senses.title: To signal with the hand
senses.definition: to make a movement of the hand or head as a sign or direction
senses.definitionCN: 用手部或头部的动作作为信号或指引
senses.example: The usher motioned us toward the side door.
senses.exampleCN: 引座员示意我们往侧门走。
senses.why: The noun became a verb: to give a motion with the hand is to motion someone.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：用手给出一个动作，就是向某人示意。

intro.en: Motion comes through Old French from Latin motio, a moving, built on the past-participle stem mot- of movere 'to move'. The proposal sense grows from bringing something forward, not from physical travel.
intro.cn: motion 经古法语来自拉丁 motio「移动」，由 movere「移动、推动」的过去分词词干 mot- 构成。动议义由「把某事提出来、推到面前」引申，并非来自物理位移。

items.en: Movere meant to move, to push away, to set in motion; its past-participle stem mot- is the base of the noun.
items.cn: movere 意为移动、推开、使动起来；它的过去分词词干 mot- 是名词的底子。

items.en: Motio, motionis named a moving or a movement; it is a third-declension noun built on the same stem.
items.cn: motio、motionis 指一次移动或运动；这是由同一词干构成的第三变格法名词。

items.en: Old French motion carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century, first as movement and soon after as a proposal.
items.cn: 古法语 motion 在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，先指移动，不久也指提议。

items.en: English motion is recorded from the fourteenth century in the plain sense of movement, and in legal use soon afterwards.
items.cn: 英语 motion 自十四世纪有「移动」的直白用法记录，随后不久进入法律语境。

items.en: The sense of a proposal grows from the idea of bringing something forward, a motion made in a room rather than in space.
items.cn: 「提议」义从「把某事提出来」这一想法长出，是在房间里而非空间中做出的动作。

items.en: The first dates of the parliamentary and legal senses are approximate; the noun is well attested from the medieval period.
items.cn: 议会义与法律义的最早记录年代为约数；这个名词在中世纪已有充分记录。

note.en: The first group shares the stem of moving; the second group separates motion from a gesture, a proposal and a trend.
note.cn: 第一组共享「移动」的词干；第二组把 motion 与手势、提议、趋势等相邻说法区分开。

entries.definition: The verb and a common noun for a single act of moving; motion is the more formal noun of the process.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，也作普通名词指一次移动；motion 是更正式、指整个过程的名词。

entries.definition: From mot- plus -ive: the reason that moves a person to act, not the act of moving.
entries.definitionCN: 由「移动」词干加表倾向的词尾构成：推动人去行动的理由，不是移动的动作。

entries.definition: Built on the same stem with an agent ending: the thing that produces movement, as an engine does.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词干加表施动者的词尾：产生运动的东西，如发动机。

entries.definition: Com- 'together' plus motion: a confused rushing about of people, a movement that is noisy.
entries.definitionCN: 表「一起」的拉丁前缀加「移动」：人群慌乱地涌动，一种喧闹的移动。

entries.definition: Not a form of motion and from a different source: it comes from a separate Latin noun for an instant or a weight, and in English it names a point in time rather than a movement.
entries.definitionCN: 不是 motion 的一种形式：它来自另一个拉丁名词，指瞬间或重量；英语中它指时间上的一点，而非移动。

entries.definition: Movement in general, often of a group or a trend; motion is more often a single act or a formal proposal.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指运动，常指一群人的行动或趋势；motion 更常指单次动作或正式动议。

entries.definition: A deliberate movement of the body that communicates; motion can be any movement, gesture is always meaningful.
entries.definitionCN: 有传达作用的身体动作；motion 可以是任何动作，gesture 一定带有意义。

entries.definition: A plan offered for consideration; a motion is a proposal put formally to a meeting.
entries.definitionCN: 提出供考虑的计划；motion 是正式提交会议表决的提议。

entries.definition: The ability to move from place to place, used of animals and vehicles rather than of processes.
entries.definitionCN: 从一处到另一处移动的能力，多用于动物与交通工具，而非抽象过程。

entries.definition: The speed at which something moves; motion names the fact of moving, not how fast.
entries.definitionCN: 移动的快慢；motion 说的是「在动」这件事，不涉及快慢。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Movere is Latin for move, and mot- is its participle stem.
normal.cn: movere 是拉丁语「移动」，mot- 是它的分词词干。

normal.en: The family runs motion, motionless, motive, motor, commotion.
normal.cn: 同族词有 motion、motionless、motive、motor、commotion。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the everyday senses: in motion, slow motion, set in motion, motion picture.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出日常义：在运动中、慢动作、启动、电影。

normal.en: Law says a motion to dismiss is a formal request, not a physical move.
normal.cn: 法律上的「撤销动议」是正式申请，不是物理移动。

normal.en: Physics describes motion with velocity and acceleration, two ways of measuring how it changes.
normal.cn: 物理用速度与加速度描述运动，这是衡量它如何变化的两种方式。

abstract.en: Picture a chess piece sliding one square, leaving a pale trail behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚棋子滑过一格，身后留下一道浅痕。

abstract.en: Picture a hand lifted at a meeting, and the room falling silent before a word is spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象会议上一只手抬起，还没开口，全场就静了。

abstract.en: Picture a key turned in a lock and a whole machine waking up.
abstract.cn: 想象钥匙在锁里一转，整台机器醒了过来。

examples.en: The motion of the tide is charted twice a day.
examples.cn: 潮水的运动每天被记录两次。

examples.en: Her motion to reopen the case was rejected.
examples.cn: 她要求重审此案的动议被驳回了。

examples.en: The camera records motion in the dark by sensing heat.
examples.cn: 这台摄像机在黑暗中靠感热来记录运动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mo（摸）+ tion（神）」——摸一下就走，身子一动；motion 运动、动议

root: 拉丁 movere「移动、推动」→ 过去分词词干 mot- → 拉丁 motio「移动」→ 古法语 motion → 英语 motion；会议动议义由「提出、推动」引申。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one push: a body changes place, a hand makes a sign, an idea is pushed before a meeting, a request before a court, a process is started, a machine runs, its works are named, and finally the hand itself becomes a verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「推」展开：身体换位、手做出信号、想法被推到会议前、申请被推到法庭前、进程被启动、机器运转、机芯得名，最后手本身变成动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger pushes a piece from one square to the next, and the piece leaves a trail.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指把棋子从一格推到下一格，棋子拖出一道痕迹。

branches.en: THE PLAIN MOVE: a body changes place, and one small move of the hand carries a message.
branches.cn: 直白的动：身体换位，而手的一个小动作传达信息。

branches.en: BROUGHT BEFORE OTHERS: the same push places a proposal before a meeting or a request before a court.
branches.cn: 推到众人面前：同一个推力把提议放到会议前，或把申请放到法庭前。

branches.en: SET GOING: a process is pushed into motion, and a machine keeps moving once it starts.
branches.cn: 使之启动：进程被推入运动，机器一旦启动便持续运转。

branches.en: THE WORKS: the parts that carry the movement inside a watch take the name of movement itself.
branches.cn: 机芯：钟表内部承担运动的那套部件，直接以「运动」命名。

branches.en: THE VERB: the hand that made the sign becomes the act of motioning.
branches.cn: 动词：做出信号的那只手，变成「示意」这个动作。

intro.en: Motion is a Latin noun of moving, and the stem mot- builds verbs, agents and a whole English family.
intro.cn: motion 是表示「移动」的拉丁名词，词干 mot- 还构成动词、施动者名词与整个英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin movere gives motio and motion, and also motive, motor, commotion and momentum; the ending -tion names an action or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 movere 衍生 motio 与 motion，也衍生 motive、motor、commotion 与 momentum；后缀 -tion 表示动作或结果。

items.example: The root supplies the push behind every sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根为每个义项提供「推」的底子。

items.example: The Latin noun names the act of moving.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词指移动这一动作。

items.example: She rose to put a motion to the committee.
items.exampleCN: 她起身向委员会提出动议。

items.example: The cat lay motionless under the chair.
items.exampleCN: 猫一动不动地躺在椅子下。

items.example: A commotion broke out at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 门口爆出一阵骚动。

items.meaning: a reason that moves a person
items.example: Curiosity was his only motive.
items.exampleCN: 好奇是他唯一的动机。

items.example: The motor turns the belt.

scene: 球场边的白板上还留着上一场比赛的圆圈和箭头，教练让队员围拢过来，指着墙上的旧照片讲起从前那场翻盘。The coach used an old photograph to motivate the players before the final.

senses.title: To give a person a reason to act
senses.definition: to make someone want to do something, especially by giving them a purpose or an incentive
senses.definitionCN: 使人愿意去做某事，尤指通过给其一个目标或动力
senses.example: Good teachers motivate students by making the subject matter feel useful.
senses.exampleCN: 好老师让学生觉得所学有用，从而激励他们。
senses.why: Latin movere meant to set in motion, and this verb was formed on motive, the inner force that starts an action, so motivate is literally to set a person moving from inside.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 movere 意为「使动起来」，这个动词由 motive（启动行动的内心力量）构成，所以 motivate 字面就是把人从内部推动起来。

senses.title: To be the reason behind an action
senses.definition: to be the reason or cause that makes an action, choice or change happen
senses.definitionCN: 成为使某个行动、选择或变化发生的理由或原因
senses.example: A wish to protect his family motivated the long move to another city.
senses.exampleCN: 想保护家人的愿望促成了他搬去另一座城市，成了这次远迁的动机。
senses.why: Once a motive is understood as an inner force, the verb can also point the other way: the force itself motivates the deed, so the wish, not the person, becomes the subject of the sentence.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把 motive 理解为一股内在力量，这个动词也能反过来指：那股力量本身促成了行动，于是句子的主语变成愿望本身，而不是人。

senses.title: To set out reasons for a decision
senses.definition: to give reasons for a decision, proposal or statement, especially in formal writing
senses.definitionCN: 为某个决定、提议或说法给出理由，尤用于正式写作
senses.example: The paper motivates its choice of method in a short opening section.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文在开头一小节里为它的方法选择提供了理由。
senses.why: A motive explains why something was done, so the derived verb took on the academic task of setting those reasons out, and motivate acquired the sense of justify.
senses.whyCN: motive 解释一件事为什么被做，于是由它派生的动词接过了学术写作里「把理由摆出来」的任务，motivate 就多了一层「论证、说明理由」的意思。

intro.en: Motivate is a nineteenth-century English coinage built on motive, which came through French from Latin movere, to move.
intro.cn: motivate 是十九世纪英语用 motive 造出来的词，而 motive 经法语来自拉丁语 movere（移动）。

items.en: Movere meant to move or to set in motion, and it supplied the verb behind motion, motive, motor and promote.
items.cn: movere 意为移动、使动起来，是 motion、motive、motor、promote 这些词背后的动词。

items.en: Its participle motus, a movement, also worked as a noun, and English later used the same stem for both physical motion and a stated reason.
items.cn: 它的分词 motus 意为「运动」，也可作名词；英语后来用同一个词干兼指身体的运动与陈述出来的理由。

items.en: Motivus meant serving to move, and medieval writers applied it to ideas and arguments that move the will rather than the body.
items.cn: motivus 意为「起推动作用的」，中世纪的作者把它用在能打动意志而非移动身体的念头与论据上。

items.en: Old French motif named a motive or a reason, and English borrowed motive in the fifteenth century as a word for what prompts action.
items.cn: 古法语 motif 指动机或理由，英语在十五世纪借入 motive，用来指促使人行动的东西。

items.en: The verb motivate is generally dated to the nineteenth century, when writers on psychology and education added -ate to motive and used it for the act of supplying a reason.
items.cn: 动词 motivate 一般认为形成于十九世纪，研究心理与教育的作者在 motive 后加 -ate，用它表示「提供理由」这件事。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin verb of moving and its English family; the near-meaning group collects verbs for pushing a person toward action or for supplying grounds.
note.cn: 形近组顺着拉丁语「移动」动词及其英语词族展开；近义组收表示推动人行动或提供理由的动词。

entries.definition: A reason that makes someone act in a particular way.
entries.definitionCN: 使人以某种方式行动的理由。

entries.definition: The act or process of moving.
entries.definitionCN: 移动的动作或过程。

entries.definition: To raise someone to a higher position, or to help something advance.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人提到更高职位，或推动某事进展。

entries.definition: A strong feeling that moves a person.
entries.definitionCN: 推动人的强烈情绪。

entries.definition: To give someone confidence or support to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 给某人信心或支持去做某事。

entries.definition: To fill someone with the desire to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人产生做某事的愿望。

entries.definition: To force or push someone into a state or action.
entries.definitionCN: 迫使或推动某人进入某种状态或行动。

entries.definition: To cause someone to do something, often quickly.
entries.definitionCN: 促使某人（往往马上）做某事。

normalIntro.en: The word stands on a Latin verb of moving, and its family keeps returning to the force that starts an action and to the reason given for it afterwards.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词立在拉丁语「移动」动词上，同族词反复回到启动行动的那股力，以及事后为行动给出的理由。

normal.en: Movere is the Latin verb to move, and motive names the force that starts the moving, so motivate is to set a person in motion.
normal.cn: movere 是拉丁语「移动」，motive 指启动移动的那股力，所以 motivate 就是把人推动起来。

normal.en: The ending -ate turns a noun or adjective into a verb of action, which is how motive became motivate in the nineteenth century.
normal.cn: -ate 这个结尾把名词或形容词变成表示动作的动词，motive 就是这样在十九世纪变成了 motivate。

normal.en: Motivation adds -ion and names the force itself, while motivator adds -or and names the person or thing that supplies it.
normal.cn: motivation 加 -ion，指那股力本身；motivator 加 -or，指提供那股力的人或物。

normal.en: De- reverses the verb, so demotivate is to take the drive away, a word that works because motivate is about a force.
normal.cn: de- 把动词反转，所以 demotivate 就是把动力拿走；这个词讲得通，正因为 motivate 说的是一股力。

normal.en: A coach, a teacher and a bonus can all be subjects of motivate, because the word cares about the reason supplied, not about who supplies it.
normal.cn: 教练、老师和奖金都可以做 motivate 的主语，因为这个词在意的是提供了什么理由，而不是谁来提供。

abstract.en: Picture a person standing still until a small light far ahead catches the eye, and the first step follows.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人原本站着不动，直到远处一点亮光吸住目光，第一步就跟着迈了出去。

abstract.en: A motive is invisible, yet it is the hinge on which a whole day of effort turns, so one small reason can move a large body.
abstract.cn: 动机看不见，却是一整天努力转动的那个铰链，所以一个小理由就能挪动一整个人。

abstract.en: To motivate is to hand someone a reason; to be motivated is to take that reason and make it your own.
abstract.cn: 激励是把一个理由交到别人手上；受到激励，则是接过这个理由并把它变成自己的。

examples.en: Good teachers motivate students by making the subject matter feel useful.
examples.cn: 好老师让学生觉得所学有用，从而激励他们。

examples.en: A wish to protect his family motivated the long move to another city.
examples.cn: 想保护家人的愿望促成了他搬去另一座城市。

examples.en: The paper motivates its choice of method in a short opening section.
examples.cn: 这篇论文在开头一小节里为它的方法选择提供了理由。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莫提为特」——莫提一个理由，就为特地去行动；记住 motivate 是激励、成为动机、说明理由。

root: 拉丁语 movere（移动）的过去分词 motus 派生出 motivus（推动的），经法语 motif 与英语 motive 后，十九世纪加 -ate 构成 motivate；同族词有 motive、motion、motor、promote、emotion。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a reason that sets a person moving; the senses divide into supplying that reason, being that reason, and stating reasons in formal prose.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是让人动起来的理由；义项分出提供这股理由、本身成为理由，以及在正式文字里陈述理由。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person standing still until a distant light pulls the first step out of them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人原本停住，远处一点光把他的第一步拉了出来。

branches.cn: 教练把一段旧事变成一个更拼命跑的理由

branches.en: a bonus that makes a team arrive early
branches.cn: 一笔让团队提前到岗的奖金

branches.cn: 想保护家人的愿望把一家人拉到新城市

branches.cn: 论文里交代为何选某种方法的一段

branches.cn: 同一个动词，既指行动背后的力，也指事后给出的说明

intro.cn: 一个拉丁语「移动」动词、它的分词、形容词 motivus，再加一小族英语词，把这个词从身体的移动带到内心的理由。
